title: Werkvoorbereider/Inkoper | Nieuwegein | Fulltime
description:
Als werkvoorbereider - inkoper heb je samen met het projectteam de vrijheid en uitdaging om een optimale invulling te geven aan de (prijs)technische uitwerking en uitvoering van een project. Je speelt een belangrijke rol in het voortraject van de bouw. Jij zorgt ervoor dat alles – van begin tot einde - goed geregeld is voor je uitvoerende collega’s, zodat zij direct aan de slag kunnen. Je maakt de planning van de werkzaamheden en zorgt ervoor dat er voldoende personeel, materiaal en materieel aanwezig zijn. Daarmee vorm je een belangrijke schakel tussen je collega’s op kantoor en op de bouwplaats. Geen dag is hetzelfde en dat maakt dit werk zo leuk en uitdagend!

Wat ga je zoal doen?

Als ervaren werkvoorbereider ben jij dé spil in het bouwproces. Vanaf de ontwerpfase tot en met de oplevering zorg jij voor een perfecte voorbereiding en begeleiding. Jouw taken bestaan onder andere uit:

  • Opstellen en bewaken van de juiste inkoopplanning en werkschema’s;
  • Je werkt nauw samen met de projectleider. Voor het bepalen van de bouwsystemen en andere mogelijkheden;
  • Het tijdig en juist inkopen van de juiste materialen en onderaannemers. Hierbij houd je het budget, de kwaliteit en natuurlijk de veiligheid in de gaten;
  • Controleren van bouwtekeningen samen met je collega op de tekenkamer;
  • Verantwoordelijk voor het bijhouden van de financiële administratie rondom de bouw, samen met de projectleider;
  • Bouwvergaderingen bijwonen samen met het projectteam;
  • Ondersteunen van de projectleider bij alle voorkomende werkzaamheden rondom jullie project;

Voor wie en waar ga je werken?

Ten Brinke is een internationale succesvolle onderneming op het gebied van projectontwikkeling, bouw en assetmanagement. In bijna 120 jaar is Ten Brinke uitgegroeid tot ontwikkelende bouwer met vestigingen in Nederland, Duitsland, Spanje, Portugal en Griekenland, die alle facetten van de onroerendgoedmarkt beheerst. Samen met circa 1400 medewerkers werken wij aan zeer diverse projecten en genereren we een gemiddelde jaaromzet van circa 1,4 miljard euro. Wij zijn een écht familiebedrijf en dat zie je terug in onze no-nonsense cultuur, onze waarden en onze platte organisatiestructuur. Optimaal voldoen aan de persoonlijke wensen en eisen van onze klant en/of partner is onze hoogste prioriteit. We streven hierbij naar een probleemloze afwikkeling van alle te doorlopen (bouw)processen.


Welke talenten en vaardigheden zien we graag?

  • Een afgeronde MBO / HBO opleiding richting bouwkunde of bouwtechnische bedrijfskunde;
  • Minimaal 5 jaar relevante werkervaring als werkvoorbereider in de bouw;
  • Een ambitie om binnen het bedrijf te groeien;
  • Goede kennis van bouwprocessen, regelgeving en technische details;
  • Je hebt uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden en weet dit op een efficiënte manier toe te passen bij alle betrokken partijen van het project, zowel in- als extern;
  • Je gaat altijd voor het beste resultaat, dit samen met het team.

Wat bieden wij jou?

  • Een goed salaris dat meegroeit met jouw ontwikkeling en een jaarlijkse winstuitkering;
  • Goede secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden zoals voldoende vakantiedagen, een goed pensioen, korting op aanvullende pakketten bij de ziektekostenverzekering en een lease a bike regeling;
  • Een laptop en mobiele telefoon van de zaak;
  • Veel aandacht voor jouw (persoonlijke) groei dankzij onze eigen Ten Brinke Academy met volop opleiding- en trainingsmogelijkheden;
  • Je werkt samen met leuke collega’s in een team met ambitie die allemaal dezelfde passie hebben voor het ontwikkelen en bouwen van projecten;
  • Een uitdagende en afwisselende functie met veel vrijheid bij een financieel zeer gezond bedrijf;

title: Senior AI Architect, Semantic Layer & Algorithm Ar
description:
Dynata is seeking a Senior AI Architect for Semantic Layer & Algorithm Architecture to lead the design of the foundational architectures that power the company's next-generation data, analytics, and AI ecosystem.

This Senior AI Architect will define the technical patterns, governance frameworks, and integration standards that connect Dynata's lakehouse, semantic layer, feature ecosystem, and machine learning capabilities into a scalable and reusable platform. Working at the intersection of data architecture, governance, and AI enablement, the Senior AI Architect will ensure that data assets are discoverable, interoperable, and optimized for analytics, machine learning, and emerging AI applications.

Reporting to the VP, Research & Data Science, this role will partner closely with product, engineering, and platform teams to establish the architectural standards that support Dynata's evolving portfolio of data products, AI capabilities, and enterprise decision-support systems.

Key Responsibilities

Semantic Layer & Data Architecture

  • Define and evolve the technical architecture for Dynata's semantic layer, medallion architecture, and enterprise data models.

  • Translate business concepts, governance standards, and domain definitions into scalable technical frameworks and enforceable architectures.

  • Establish standards for schema design, metadata management, interoperability, and semantic consistency across the platform.

  • Ensure analytical, operational, and AI use cases are supported by a common architectural foundation.

Data Contracts & Governance Standards

  • Design and govern data contract frameworks that enable reliable, reusable, and trusted data assets across the organization.

  • Establish standards for schema validation, versioning, lineage, quality controls, and controlled evolution of enterprise datasets.

  • Partner with governance stakeholders to operationalize policies through technical controls and platform capabilities.

  • Promote consistency, traceability, and discoverability across enterprise data assets.

AI & Algorithm Platform Architecture

  • Define architectural patterns for feature stores, model inputs and outputs, model lifecycle management, and algorithm interoperability.

  • Establish standards for how analytical models, machine learning solutions, and AI services integrate with enterprise data assets.

  • Design scalable frameworks for feature reuse, model governance, and algorithm deployment.

  • Ensure AI and machine learning capabilities are built upon secure, governed, and reusable platform foundations.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner closely with Product, Technology, Research & Data Science, and Data Platform teams.

  • Translate complex technical concepts into clear architectural decisions and implementation guidance.

  • Lead architecture discussions that balance business needs, governance requirements, technical feasibility, and long-term scalability.

  • Serve as a technical thought leader on semantic architecture, data governance, AI enablement, and enterprise platform design.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in data architecture, platform architecture, AI/ML infrastructure, data engineering, or related fields.

  • Proven experience designing enterprise-scale semantic layers, data models, schema governance frameworks, or data contract architectures.

  • Strong understanding of modern lakehouse architectures, medallion design patterns, metadata management, and data governance principles.

  • Demonstrated experience architecting machine learning and AI platforms, including feature stores, model lifecycle management, lineage, and governance capabilities.

  • Experience establishing technical standards that support analytics, machine learning, and AI-driven applications at scale.

  • Strong understanding of schema management, metadata frameworks, versioning strategies, and interoperability patterns.

  • Experience translating ambiguous business requirements and governance concepts into scalable technical architectures.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including experience influencing technical leaders, architects, and executive stakeholders.

  • Demonstrated success operating effectively in ambiguous environments and leading foundational platform and architecture initiatives.

  • Experience with modern data and AI platforms such as Databricks, DataHub, Snowflake, feature stores, metadata platforms, or comparable technologies.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience implementing or governing enterprise semantic layers and business glossaries.

  • Familiarity with AI governance, model governance, and responsible AI frameworks.

  • Experience designing architecture for graph analytics, forecasting, optimization, or decision-support systems.

  • Exposure to LLM-enabled platform capabilities such as metadata generation, semantic modeling, catalog enrichment, or governance automation.

At Dynata, we deliver the highest quality first-party data to help businesses around the world gain precise insights, activate the right audiences, and confidently measure impact. With industry-leading respondent accuracy, reliability, and a commitment to continuous improvement, Dynata is the trusted foundation for smarter decision-making.

Northpoint Recovery Holdings, LLC began 2009 as Ashwood Outpatient and officially launched the Northpoint platform in 2015. Now celebrating 10 years of growth in 2025, Northpoint is a leading behavioral healthcare provider offering evidence-based treatment for adults with substance use and co-occurring disorders through the Northpoint Recovery brand, and mental health treatment for adolescents through Imagine by Northpoint. Operating under an in-network, commercial insurance model, Northpoint has grown exclusively through de novo expansion—from two facilities to seventeen across the Western U.S.—with more planned in both existing and new markets. We’re guided by core values of humility, heart, inspiration, and conviction. Our mission is simple: saving lives and restoring relationships by helping people get their lives back, and treating every individual with empathy and respect.

POSITION SUMMARY: As a member of the Northpoint team, the Recovery Technician is responsible for attending to the safety and wellbeing of patients, and working with a multidisciplinary treatment team in accordance with policy and procedure, to provide the best possible patient care. This position plays an important role in the implementation of programming and care plans by providing direct and indirect patient care that complies with Northpoint policies and procedures for unlicensed staff. This position will actively support the structure of the milieu through appropriate resource allocation and supervision of patients. The Recovery Technician works in a variety of settings throughout the week, including onsite at the facility and other community activities.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES:

  • Interact routinely with patients, observe behaviors and communicate significant observations to clinical staff
  • Follow reporting and communication guidelines when interacting with staff and patients
  • Timely completion and accuracy of paperwork, including daily logs and forms
  • Maintains daily schedules and structure, specifically around transport times, meal times, transition times, and others outside of normal programming hours
  • Function as a member of the treatment team and provide patient observation rounds, and consistent monitoring of patient’s activities and behaviors during scheduled shift
  • Attend and actively promote recreational outings and activities with patients; encourage pro-social and coping skills
  • Ensure the wellbeing of patients and provide a positive, supportive, and structured environment; proactively respond to patient needs to improve outcomes and the overall patient experience
  • Ensure facility cleanliness and upkeep under direction of leadership
  • Assist patients with their needs and collaborate with onsite clinical and medical staff as necessary
  • Facilitate and assist with selected activity and education group sessions; document timely and accurately according to established policies and procedures
  • Oversee and manage the safe and efficient transport of patients to and from our facilities
  • Assist in orientation of new admissions
  • Utilize therapeutic communication skills and maintain professional boundaries with patients and their families
  • Be a role model for patients and create a positive culture with staff by emulating professional attitude, language, and communication
  • Assist with treatment planning and discharge planning
  • Document information regarding client care and behavior as required in established policies and procedures

title: Head Psychologist: Autism & Developmental Diagnostics
description:
FronteraCare delivers life-changing autism services to children and families across New Mexico and Colorado. We provide high quality diagnostic evaluations and ABA therapy, partnering closely with parents, grandparents, foster parents, and other caregivers to create individualized care plans rooted in each child's unique strengths, needs, and family context.

Our clinicians are committed to evidence-based, compassionate care that helps children with autism thrive. We believe the best outcomes are when families are at the heart of the treatment. By combining clinical expertise with family insights, we help children build skills, gain confidence, and thrive.

Our Mission
Our mission is to expand access to exceptional diagnostic and behavioral healthcare for every child, no matter where they live or their circumstances.

Frontera is reimagining how children with autism and other behavioral health needs get the care they deserve. We bring together world-class clinicians, technologists, and autism specialists to build cutting-edge AI tools that help care teams work smarter and spend more time with the children and families who need them most.

Our platform is HIPAA-compliant and designed for the real-world needs of behavioral health teams — from psychologists to ABA therapists. By combining evidence-based care with powerful technology, we're expanding access to high-quality services for families everywhere.

Our Mission

Frontera exists to close the care gap: every child, no matter where they live, should be able to access effective behavioral healthcare.

Why Join Us

At Frontera, you'll join a team driven by impact. We're growing quickly, backed by leading investors, and united by a shared belief that innovation and equity can change lives. If you're excited to build the future of pediatric healthcare, we'd love to meet you.

Role Overview

As Lead Psychologist, Autism & Developmental Diagnostics, you'll be the clinical and operational anchor for Frontera's telehealth diagnostic team. You'll ensure every autism and developmental evaluation meets a consistently high bar for quality, while helping your team find smarter, more efficient ways to work, because time saved without sacrificing quality means another child gets answers sooner. You'll carry a small evaluation caseload of your own, and spend the rest of your time developing your team, strengthening clinical standards, and partnering closely with Operations, Intake, and Product to build a diagnostic program that's both excellent and built to scale.

This is a role for someone who can hold two things in tension: the clinical rigor and individualized care every family deserves, and the efficiency Frontera needs to reach more of the families who need us. You'll set the standard for what “good” looks like on both fronts and you'll be comfortable making real tradeoffs, and helping your team make them too.

What You'll Do

Clinical Leadership & Quality

  • Serve as the go-to resource for clinical questions, screener guidance, and evaluation standards across the diagnostics team
  • Set and uphold consistent standards for clinical quality, complex case decision-making, report writing, and neuroaffirming language
  • Review evaluations and consult on complex or atypical cases
  • Define best practices for accessible, high-quality telehealth autism and developmental evaluation
  • Carry a modest caseload of your own (about two evaluations per week) to stay grounded in the work
  • Set clear, explicit guidance on where the line is between more time meaning more quality, and more time meaning a family waits longer for a diagnosis and help your team make that call with confidence

Team Support & Development

  • Lead onboarding, training, and calibration for new psychologists and speech-language pathologists
  • Support your team's ongoing growth and skill development
  • Run regular 1:1s and team meetings that keep people aligned, supported, and unstuck
  • Own change management for new tools, processes, and programs across the team
  • Set clear expectations and hold your team accountable to them — with warmth, and without avoiding the hard conversations when they're needed

Operational Alignment

  • Partner with Intake and Operations to build workflows, scheduling, and communication that actually work
  • Spot the operational gaps that get in the way of quality or efficiency, and help fix them
  • Turn good clinical ideas into concrete, sequenced plans, with real metrics and timelines, not just principles

Product & Technology Partnership

  • Partner closely with Engineering and Product on report tools, documentation templates, and workflows
  • Bring specific, proactive ideas for where technology could save time without costing quality — you don't just flag problems, you help solve them
  • Help identify, track, and prioritize product issues with clear clinical context
  • Partner with Customer Success to close the loop between client experience and clinical practice

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Represent the clinical point of view in conversations about scaling, tooling, and how we design our services
  • Help hire, evaluate, and calibrate new psychologists and speech-language pathologists
  • Advocate for standardized, scalable workflows where they help us serve more families, even when that means less case-by-case customization
  • Contribute to quality improvement and clinical governance efforts

Travel

  • Occasional travel to New Mexico and other markets for team training, calibration, and partnership-building
  • Frequent visits to our Denver headquarters to stay connected with the clinical operations team

Who You Are

  • A doctoral-level psychologist with deep experience in autism and developmental evaluation
  • Skilled in telehealth-based assessment, with strong clinical judgment, report writing, and ADOS (Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule) administration
  • Experienced training, mentoring, and leading interdisciplinary clinical teams
  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity and building consistency in a fast-growing environment
  • Experienced managing the performance of licensed clinicians serving underserved communities
  • A natural partner to technologists and product teams — you can talk concretely about where tools and workflows intersect with clinical quality, not just work around what exists
  • Someone who makes good decisions under time pressure, not only when things are calm
  • Comfortable standardizing and scaling processes, and willing to prioritize consistency when it's what's best for the most families
  • An assertive, steady leader who can set a clear standard for a team and hold to it

What Success Looks Like

  • Clinicians have a reliable go-to person for day-to-day questions and support
  • Evaluation quality is consistent, timely, and meets gold-standard practices
  • Workflows between Ops, Intake, and Clinical run smoothly
  • New clinicians ramp up quickly with strong support
  • A cohesive team culture aligned with our mission to close the care gap
  • A well-maintained library of clinical SOPs and documentation
  • Clear, measurable improvements in quality and/or throughput — not just team morale
  • A strong, trusted working relationship with Product and Engineering, built on specific and proactive ideas

Why Frontera Health?

  • Help shape the future of pediatric behavioral healthcare
  • Lead and grow a clinical team at a company built to close the care gap
  • Join a mission-driven team backed by leading investors
  • Make a real, measurable difference in the lives of children and families who need care
  • Competitive compensation and benefits package

Join us in building the future of behavioral healthcare.

We have determined a salary range for this position that takes into account several factors including experience, knowledge, education, skills, and abilities. Please note that the salary information is a general guideline and the exact salary will be determined based on the individual’s qualifications and experience, with consideration given to the factors listed above. All full-time employee benefits include health benefits, 401(k) plan, and PTO per year.

Compensation
$175,000—$200,000 USD

Why Join Us
At Frontera Care, you will be part of a mission-driven, supportive team making a real difference for children and families. We provide the tools, resources, collaboration you need to focus on what matters most: delivering high-quality, family-centered care. If you are passionate about helping children with autism, and want to grow your career while transforming access to care, accessible healthcare, we would love to welcome you to our team.

title: Professional Counselor I-II, University Counseling Center
description:
Job Title

Professional Counselor I-II, University Counseling Center

Agency

Texas A&M University - Corpus Christi

Department

University Counseling

Proposed Minimum Salary

Commensurate

Job Location

Corpus Christi, Texas

Job Type

Staff

Job Description

TAMU-CC is a dynamic university designated as both a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) and Minority-Serving Institution (MSI) with approximately 11,000 students from 47 states and 54 foreign nations. We employ over 1,400 full-time and 2,000 part-time Islanders (including students/GAs). The University attracts highly talented faculty and staff and offers an array of undergraduate and graduate degrees, including doctoral programs. As a member of the Texas A&M University System, TAMU-CC benefits from a range of resources, increased visibility and influence, and opportunities to collaborate in mutually beneficial ways with peers across member institutions and associated agencies.

TAMU-CC’s beautiful campus is located on a 240-acre island on Corpus Christi Bay and was ranked #1 College by the Sea by Best College Reviews. Our natural setting is enhanced by its modern, attractive, and state-of-the-art classroom buildings and support facilities.

PURPOSE

The Professional Counselor I/II serves the Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi community by providing a full continuum of psychological services with a specialized focus on crisis intervention, triage assessment, and alcohol and other drug (AOD) screening and programming. Under general supervision, this position delivers individual and group counseling, comprehensive clinical/triage assessments, clinical supervision, and outreach/consultation.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Functional Area 1: Clinical Services

Percent Effort: 25%

  • Provide brief individual counseling, consultation, and referrals.

  • Conduct alcohol and drug screenings and comprehensive substance use assessments.

  • Facilitate recovery-focused group sessions, psychoeducational classes, and support groups, as assigned.

  • Maintain accurate/timely documentation in the electronic medical records system.

  • Participate in biweekly case conferences and informal case consultations for client care coordination.

Functional Area 2: Crisis/Triage Consultation

Percent Effort: 40%

  • Conduct triage and crisis assessments including de-escalation, safety/risk evaluation, and stabilization planning during daily crisis walk-in hours.

  • Coordinate referrals to a higher level of care (inpatient hospitalization, intensive outpatient, etc.) as needed.

  • Follow up with students in crisis to monitor progress and ensure linkage to support.

Functional Area 3: Consultation & Outreach

Percent Effort: 15%

  • Develop and deliver presentations, workshops, and outreach programs related to mental health, suicide prevention, and AOD issues.

  • Engage in campus-wide prevention and early intervention efforts.

  • Serve as liaison and consultant to campus and community partners, including collegiate recovery/programming initiatives.

  • Provide short-term embedded support services in conjunction with campus programs including occasional weekend and evening programs (e.g., annual university camp for freshman).

Functional Area 4: Program Coordination

Percent Effort: 10%

  • Coordinate a specialized program area (e.g., AOD, recovery programming, embedded support for specific student population).

  • Collaborate with campus partners to optimize care coordination and referral pathways.

Functional Area 5: Clinical Supervision

Percent Effort: 10%

  • Provide clinical supervision to master’s level counseling practicum trainees and interns.

  • Participate in selection, onboarding, and training of counseling practicum trainees and interns.

QUALIFICATIONS

Professional Counselor I:

  • Master’s degree in Counseling, Clinical Psychology, Social Work or other specialty related to job function.

  • Practical/field placement relevant to college counseling, or supervised experience related to job function.

  • Licensed as Licensed Professional Counselor Associate. Must maintain licensure for continued employment.

Professional Counselor II:

  • Master’s degree in counseling, Clinical Psychology, Social Work or other specialty related to job function.

  • Texas Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC), Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT), or Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW). Must maintain licensure for continued employment.

  • LPC’s must have completed at least 3000 hours of post-licensure clinical mental health experience in no less than 18 months of supervision. LMFT’s must have completed 3000 clock hours of full-time post-licensure clinical experience in no less than 24 months with 200 hours of supervision. LCSW’s must have completed at least one (1) year of supervised clinical experience with 100 hours of supervision and have passed their state board exam.

OTHER REQUIRED SKILLS AND ABILITIES

  • Demonstrated experience in brief therapy and/or solution focused therapy with adults in an outpatient setting.

  • Demonstrated experience assessing and treating a wide variety of clinical conditions.

  • Demonstrated experience in crisis intervention.

  • Strong interpersonal communication skills (verbal and written) to be able to effectively collaborate within a multidisciplinary environment and the campus community.

  • Knowledge and experience with Electronic Medical Records systems

  • Knowledge and experience with telemental health platforms and providing telemental health services.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Licensed as Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) in the state of Texas or able to obtain this licensure in Texas within six months of hire if licensed in another state.

  • Two (2) or more years of post-graduate experience in social work, counseling, or other mental health agency.

  • Experience providing counseling services as a professional staff member in a university setting.

  • Experience in assessment and intervention of individuals with serious mental health concerns and/or a history of trauma.

  • Demonstrated program development and coordination skills.

  • Advanced clinical training and experience in specialized area (e.g., trauma, eating disorders, OCD, AOD)

  • Advanced clinical training, experience and certification in an evidence-based therapy modality (e.g., EMDR, DBT, ACT, CBT).

  • Experience providing clinical supervision to master’s level counseling and psychology trainees utilizing a multiculturally competent approach.

SALARY: $49,000 – $60,000/annually, approximately

  • $4,083.34 - $5,000/monthly

  • Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications.

NOTE: Employment may be impacted by the Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025 and the moratorium issued by Texas Governor Abbott on January 27, 2026.

BENEFITS (rules, policies, eligibility apply)

From our generous benefits package and professional development opportunities, to our retirement programs and our commitment to service excellence, the Island University is an engaging and rewarding place to work.

Insurance

  • Medical

    • $0 - $30 per month for Employee Only coverage after university contribution ($920 value).

    • Up to 83% of premium covered by the university:

      • Employee and Spouse

      • Employee and Children

      • Employee and Family coverage

  • Dental & Vision

  • Life Insurance, Accidental D&D, Long Term Disability, Flexible Spending Account and Day Care Spending Account

On-campus wellness opportunities

Work Life Solutions:

  • Counseling, Work Life Assistance, Financial Resources, and Legal Resources

Tuition Benefits:

  • Public Loan Forgiveness

  • Book scholarships

  • 100% tuition coverage for up to 18 credit hours per fiscal year (other rules may apply).

Retirement

  • Teacher Retirement System of Texas (TRS) or Optional Retirement Plan (ORP)

  • Voluntary Tax Deferred Account/Deferred Compensation Plan

Time Off:

  • 8+ hours of vacation paid time off every month.

  • 8 hours of sick leave time off every month.

  • 8 hours of paid time off for Birthday leave.

  • 12-15 paid holidays each year.

All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check.

title: Senior Market Fundamental Analyst
description:
Chevron is accepting online applications for the position of Senior Market Fundamental Analyst through September 14th at 11:59 p.m.

We are seeking a highly skilled and market-savvy analyst with deep expertise in the NGL, LPG, and petrochemical trading space to join our analytics team. This role focuses on developing forward-looking market views, building robust supply-demand models, and delivering actionable insights to support trading and strategic decisions across NGL, LPG, and petrochemical markets.

Responsibilities for this position may include but are not limited to:

Market Expertise & Analysis

  • Provide in-depth analysis of NGL, LPG, and petrochemical markets, including propane, butane, ethylene, propylene, and other key products for a 2–5 year time frame.

  • Interpret price movements and market dynamics, incorporating macroeconomic events, geopolitical developments, and headline risks on a 2–5 year time frame.

  • Monitor and assess market drivers and their impact on mid-term price trends.

Modeling & Forecasting

  • Build and maintain supply-demand forecast models for NGL, LPG, and petrochemicals with a 2–5 year horizon for global market with Asia focus.

  • Run scenario analyses to evaluate market outcomes under varying conditions (e.g., policy shifts, demand shocks, plant outages).

  • Lead and provide monthly market updates for 2–5 years and collaborate with short-term CAs to provide market insights.

  • Lead and provide ad-hoc market analysis for headline analysis.

Communication & Reporting

  • Write clear, concise, and insightful market reports tailored for traders and senior stakeholders.

  • Collaborate closely with trading desks to align analytics with commercial strategies.

  • Present findings and recommendations in internal forums and strategy discussions.

Technical Skills

  • Strong proficiency in Excel for data analysis and visualization.

  • Experience with Python for modeling, automation, and data manipulation is preferred.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Economics, Engineering, Finance, or a related field.

  • Over 5 years of relevant experience in NGL/LPG/petrochemical trading, market analysis, or related roles.

  • Proven track record of building market models and delivering strategic insights.

  • Ability to work independently and as part of a cross-functional team.

  • Strong communication and storytelling skills to translate complex data into actionable insights.

Relocation is not offered for this role. Only local candidates will be considered.

Expatriate assignments will not be considered.

title: Director of IT
description:
Director of Information Technology

Quindar is looking for a Director of IT to lead and scale our corporate IT function. This is a hands-on player-coach role responsible for delivering reliable, secure, and responsive IT support across our unclassified environment.

This role owns Tier 1 and Tier 2 support, employee onboarding/offboarding, endpoint management, office IT, enterprise software administration, remote employee support, and execution of CUI hardening requirements. It does not own classified or SCIF networks but will work closely with IT Engineering and Cybersecurity.

We view IT as a customer-service organization. Success means employees trust the IT team, commitments are met, issues are permanently resolved, and leadership has clear visibility into performance and priorities.

What You’ll Own

· Lead and scale the corporate IT team while remaining hands-on when needed. If you do not want to get your hands dirty, this position is not for you.

· Establish measurable SLAs and build a culture of responsive, proactive support where employees never have to chase IT for status.

· Standardize IT systems, configurations, tools, and processes to improve reliability and scalability.

· Manage an agile team including sprint planning, backlog review, and daily standups in support of enterprise projects such as GCC-H migration

· Own the IT roadmap and major projects with clear milestones, owners, risks, committed dates, and consistent stakeholder communication.

· Drive permanent fixes through root-cause analysis rather than recurring workarounds.

· Own onboarding, offboarding, endpoints, identity and access, enterprise software tools, office technology, and remote employee support.

· Partner with Cybersecurity to execute CUI hardening, patching, endpoint compliance, and related controls.

· Own incident response for corporate IT issues, including clear communication and follow-through through resolution.

· Build the on-site IT capability needed to support Quindar’s growth in Washington, DC.

· Hold the team and vendors accountable for service quality, execution, and outcomes.

What We’re Looking For

· Organized and assertive leader who will mentor and grow a team

· Experience leading corporate IT in a growing technology, aerospace, defense, government contracting, or similarly complex organization.

· Strong background in Tier 1/2 support, endpoint management, identity and access, enterprise software administration, and office IT.

· Proven ability to manage people, projects, vendors, and competing priorities while remaining technically hands-on.

· Strong customer-service mindset with high standards for communication, ownership, and follow-through.

· Experience with CUI, NIST SP 800-171, or CMMC is preferred.

What Success Looks Like

Employees trust IT. Systems are reliable – problems are fixed not patched. SLAs are met. Projects ship when promised. The team communicates clearly, owns outcomes, and scales with the company. IT is as elite as the engineers.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Sr. Sales Engineer
description:
Who is Forcepoint?

Forcepoint simplifies security for global businesses and governments. Forcepoint’s all-in-one, truly cloud-native platform makes it easy to adopt Zero Trust and prevent the theft or loss of sensitive data and intellectual property no matter where people are working. 20+ years in business. 2.7k employees. 150 countries. 11k+ customers. 300+ patents. If our mission excites you, you’re in the right place; we want you to bring your own energy to help us create a safer world. All we’re missing is you!

Forcepoint has a fantastic opportunity to join our team in Vietnam.

This is a pre-sales engineering position where you will be working extremely closely with sales. You are expected to work as team to create and execute a territory / account plan. This includes building relationships with partners and ensuring they can position and implement our solutions.

From a technology perspective we are looking for someone ideally with a Web, CASB, ZTNA and data protection security background, with experience on positioning security products on large customers. You will be joining a great, successful team of SEs in the APAC who will be happy to bring you up to speed. While we are responsible and accountable for our patch – we support and help each other, and only good team players will succeed.

Like the industry and our customers, we are transitioning from network and data security products to a “Data-First” SASE architecture. Not all companies are moving at the same speed and many continue with our really good NGFW, DLP, Web Security and other products. You should feel at home in both worlds.

What you will be doing:

  • Lead discussions with customers to drive understanding and documentation of the customer’s environment and needs, specifically their cross domain, network security, DLP/Intellectual property protection needs and recommend appropriate products/services that meet these needs.

  • Deliver product, technology and/or customized solution presentations to technical and business decision makers which may include system demonstrations, white-boarding and technical Q&A sessions to the client.

  • Provide pre-sales technical support, security engineering and technical guidance for the development and implementation of Forcepoint cybersecurity technologies for customer.

  • Work with customer, strategic partners, resellers and Forcepoint team members to architect, design, build, and deploy cyber security solutions for customers and partners in support of pilot and proof of concept demonstrations.

  • Attend industry conferences, trade shows and sales events and participate in related activities.

  • Prepare, write, and present trade studies, cost benefit analyses, white papers, reports and briefings as required.

  • Work with account managers and proposal team to develop technical content and diagrams for RFI/RFP responses

  • Orchestrate Product Specialists involvement during pre-sales activities

  • Collaborate with partners and professional services to design projects activities in order to have them aligned with customer expectations

  • Assist with maintaining state of the art demonstration and lab capabilities and other duties and projects as assigned.

    What you can bring:

  • Previous demonstrated experience within cyber security

  • Pre-sales experience working directly with cyber security and/or network products in a team environment.

  • Experience with Web security

  • Experience with Data Loss Prevention projects, approach and logic

  • Strong customer relation/engagement skills

  • Ideally have experience working with enterprise accounts

  • Confident communicator, able to proactively engage with customer.

  • Ability to effectively communicate with a broad range of audiences; from deeply technical to high executive C-level decision makers.

  • Must be able to collaboratively coordinate across traditional engineering disciplines, management and customers.

  • Knowledge of networking topology, TCP/IP protocol, proxies infrastructures, Network architectures, and components (firewalls, routers, etc.)

  • Linux/Windows systems administration experience preferred

  • Strong understanding of customers and prospects requirements, security design and system architectures

  • Experience with cyber security engineering projects and programs

  • Experience with Vietnam cyber security markets preferred

  • Fluent in English communication required

Don’t meet every single qualification? Studies show people are hesitant to apply if they don’t meet all requirements listed in a job posting. Forcepoint is focused on building an inclusive and diverse workplace – so if there is something slightly different about your previous experience, but it otherwise aligns and you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply. You could be a great candidate for this or other roles on our team.

title: Member of GTM Staff - New York
description:
Beacon is building the essential technology infrastructure for the everyday economy: the businesses, organizations, and services that make real life work, and that mainstream tech has largely left behind. We acquire, operate, and grow vertical market software companies. They are niche, founder-built businesses serving industries that are often overlooked and too profitable to ignore.

Our model is simple: we seek out founders who have built their business by spending years understanding their market and prioritizing their customers' specific needs. We buy great businesses, invest in their continued growth, and hold them permanently, accelerating that growth with an AI-native platform built specifically for vertical market software. No mandate to cut, flip, or roll up into something unrecognizable.

We are not a financial firm. We are technology entrepreneurs and operators who believe the most important businesses in the world are already running quietly in industries most people never think about. Our job is to find them, support the people who built them, and make them better.

Beacon is backed by a diverse base of investors, with $550M+ raised to date, including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp, and evergreen funds built for the long game.

About the Role

Beacon Software buys businesses. You get to grow them. This can take almost any shape. Here are real projects our team ran over the last few months:

  • Launched ads across Meta and Google.

  • Ran a full outbound process (leadgen, copywriting, outreach) on behalf of a sales team.

  • Vibecoded an interactive TAM map to figure out which states and provinces to prioritize.

  • Designed and launched landing pages.

  • Built a system to flag high-dollar accounts at risk of churning.

  • Cross-sold into other portfolio companies.

  • Gameplanned a conference.

  • Prototyped a programmatic SEO strategy.

  • (And much more!)

Want some industry jargon? You’ll be a fractional head of growth (a forward-deployed GTM engineer?) who goes deep into portfolio companies and brainstorms, prioritizes, and executes on growth experiments.

We’re looking for an animal who can go into a business, ask the right questions with little context, launch experiments, and drive revenue.

Basically, we’re looking for The Wolf, but for growth.

Why would you want this role?

  • Get a first-person view into the world of private equity, rollups, and AI.

  • Access proprietary learnings about vertical SaaS businesses in a variety of industries.

  • Work with a team of former YC founders, growth leaders, and execs at Silicon Valley’s fastest-growing companies like Instacart, AngelList, Coinbase, and Retool.

  • Have loads of control and autonomy over what you work on.

  • Be artsy AND sciencey.

    • Like writing copy and brainstorming video ideas? You get to do that.

    • Like reading investment memos and deeply understanding businesses? You get to do that, too.

  • Go deep and broad.

    • We have an $8M ARR company that we think can get to $100M with intelligent performance marketing.

    • We also have a $1M ARR company that has never had a formal growth strategy.

  • Spend an ample LLM token budget.

  • Earn meaningful equity in a hyperscaler that’s already profitable.

Who are you?

You’re probably one of these:

  • A growth hire at a startup who wants to get back to early-stage work and ship things.

  • A former founder who took their company from 0 to 1.

  • An agency owner or growth consultant sick of doing their own BD, but who enjoys the day-to-day work. (Run an agency? We’re open to acquihiring your team!)

Additionally:

  • You write clearly and concisely.

  • You’ve cracked a growth channel or loop before. You have delivered value.

  • You try things yourself to know what “good” looks like before you outsource them.

  • You’re skeptical of vanity metrics.

  • You vibecode enough to be dangerous, but you’re not a man-with-a-hammer.

  • You’re broadly curious about how businesses work.

  • You like to ship.

  • You don’t like meetings.

How is this role different from the other growth lead role you posted?

You caught us; it’s functionally the same. We’re testing different job descriptions and recruiting pipelines to figure out what attracts the best people.

(As you can probably tell, we don’t really care about titles.)

Have recommendations on what we should test? Include them in your application! Part of your job will be growing our team, too. The one minor difference is that the growth lead role is for a couple specific pods, whereas this role is more pod-agnostic. It’s a slightly different recruiting process.

Key responsibilities

  • Meet with group CPOs and portfolio company GMs, marrying product direction with user learnings to brainstorm growth experiments.

  • Prioritize, build, and launch experiments that meaningfully drive revenue.

  • Identify and optimize growth loops at portfolio companies.

  • Track and improve conversion at every major step of the marketing funnel.

  • Build systems (e.g., playbooks, Claude skills, mini-products) that less technical folks can use to run GTM experiments themselves.

  • Hire other great growth people.


Our Values at Beacon Software

  • Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.

  • Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.

  • Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected.

  • Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.


How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process: To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Beacon Software uses Artificial Intelligence and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.

AI does not make hiring decisions: Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

title: Senior Engineer- Agentic AI
description:
Job Description:

At Bank of America, we are guided by a common purpose to help make financial lives better through the power of every connection. We do this by driving Responsible Growth and delivering for our clients, teammates, communities and shareholders every day.

Being a Great Place to Work is core to how we drive Responsible Growth. At Bank of America, you can build a successful career with opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact. Join us!

Job Description:
This job is responsible for defining and leading the engineering approach for complex features to deliver significant business outcomes. Key responsibilities of the job include delivering complex features and technology, enabling development efficiencies, providing technical thought leadership based on conducting multiple software implementations, and applying both depth and breadth in a number of technical competencies. Additionally, this job is accountable for end-to-end solution design and delivery.

Position Summary:

We’re seeking a Senior Engineer to lead the design and implementation of Agentic AI across the SDLC. You will define the strategy, architecture, and operating model for applying GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry, and the Microsoft Agentic Framework—enhanced by RAG, context engineering, prompt engineering, and knowledge graphs—to automate and elevate developer workflows from planning through production. You will partner with product, platform, risk, and delivery teams to drive measurable outcomes, ensure responsible use, and scale adoption across the enterprise.

Responsibilities:

Strategy & Roadmap:

- Define the enterprise Agentic‑AI‑in‑SDLC strategy, operating model, and multiyear roadmap, aligning with business objectives, enterprise architecture, and developer‑productivity goals.

- Prioritize epics and features in the backlog and drive cross‑portfolio execution to accelerate value realization and adoption.

Architecture & Design:

- Architect agentic workflows using the Microsoft Agentic Framework and integrate them with SDLC systems including issue trackers, repositories, CI/CD pipelines, quality and security gates, and observability platforms.

- Design context architecture—grounding data, state management, retrieval patterns, prompt templates, and caching—to ensure reliable, high‑quality outcomes. - Design RAG solutions using enterprise content, vector search, and knowledge graphs, and define reference architectures and guardrails for Copilot‑based coding, testing, and automation.

Engineering & Delivery:

- Lead delivery of AI agents that automate SDLC tasks such as requirements analysis, design reviews, test generation, traceability, code‑quality enforcement, documentation updates, and release readiness.

- Build Copilots with Copilot Studio, integrating plugins, enterprise search, and workflow actions, and operationalize models in Azure AI Foundry with full lifecycle support for evaluation, monitoring, safety, and CI/CD/CT pipelines for prompts and agents.

Data, RAG, and Knowledge Graphs:

- Define ontology and schema for domain knowledge graphs and integrate code metadata, service catalogs, architectural decisions, and control libraries to create robust retrieval ecosystems.

- Implement strong data governance for retrieval sources, ensuring correct handling of sensitive data, adherence to residency and retention rules, and delivery of high‑quality grounding pipelines.

LLMOps / MLOps:

- Establish LLMOps practices including prompt/version management, evaluation suites for quality, safety, bias, and hallucination, and offline/online experiments such as A/B tests.

- Maintain golden datasets and benchmarks aligned to SDLC goals like code‑quality improvement, vulnerability reduction, and MTTR reduction.

Security, Compliance & Risk:

- Partner with Risk, Legal, Privacy, InfoSec, and Model Risk to define responsible‑AI patterns including policy‑as‑code controls, auditable logs, data‑boundary enforcement, content safety, and human‑in‑the‑loop review.

- Navigate governance and control processes to ensure solutions meet regulatory and model‑risk expectations.

Change Management & Adoption:

- Lead developer onboarding, enablement, and communities of practice by sharing prompt patterns, reusable tools, and exemplars.

- Track and communicate value through KPIs and OKRs and provide progress updates and insights to executive stakeholders

Required Qualifications:

  • 10+ years in software engineering/architecture with 2+ years leading AI/LLM or intelligent automation solutions in production, ideally at enterprise scale.

  • Proven experience implementing Agentic AI solutions (tool‑use orchestration, planning, memory/state) and integrating them with SDLC platforms.

  • Hands‑on with GitHub Copilot (org‑level policies, telemetry, governance), Microsoft Copilot Studio (plugins/connectors), and Azure AI Foundry (Prompt Flow, eval/monitoring, safety and compliance).

  • Deep knowledge of RAG, prompt & context engineering, and vector search; experience building knowledge graphs and integrating them into retrieval workflows.

  • Strong grasp of LLMOps/MLOps: dataset curation, eval design, regression testing for prompts/agents, observability, safety/guardrails, rollout strategies.

  • Expertise with SDLC toolchains: GitHub, CI/CD, IaC, testing frameworks, SAST/DAST, artifact repositories, service catalogs, and runbooks.

  • Ability to lead cross‑functional programs, manage risk, and communicate with executive and engineering stakeholders.

  • Familiarity with responsible AI principles, data privacy, and secure software development practices.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Experience in regulated industries and with Model Risk Management or similar governance.

  • Knowledge of enterprise search, graph databases, and metadata management.

  • Background with cloud platforms (Azure preferred), container orchestration (Kubernetes), and policy‑as‑code.

  • Exposure to evaluation techniques (task success, safety, toxicity, grounding fidelity, hallucination rates) and A/B testing for agents.

40

title: Bearing Engineer
description:
About the Role

Job ID

300019

Location

Denmark

Midtjylland

Brande

Company

Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy A/S

Organization

Wind Power

Business Unit

Onshore

Full / Part time

Full Time or Part Time

Experience Level

Professional / Experienced

A Snapshot of Your Day

Join our Bearings team within the Mechanical Drive Train unit, where your expertise will play a crucial role in ensuring business continuity. Imagine diving deep into the technical intricacies of bearing failures, conducting thorough Root Cause Analysis (RCA) to uncover failure modes and mechanisms. You will engage in hands-on inspections and collaborate with key stakeholders, delivering detailed reports that drive quality improvements. You will work both independently and collaboratively with colleagues globally to resolve complex technical challenges. Your expertise directly contributes to improving turbine availability and ensuring sustainable energy production for communities worldwide.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • You will conduct comprehensive Root Cause Analysis (RCA) on failed wind turbine bearings identifying critical failure modes and mechanisms.
  • Perform hands-on visual and metallurgic inspections of failed bearings and associated components in a workshop environment.
  • Analyze operational data, maintenance history, and design specifications to support thorough failure investigations.
  • Develop and document detailed technical reports summarizing your investigation findings for both internal and external stakeholders.
  • Present and discuss RCA findings and technical recommendations with customers and suppliers.

What You Bring

  • You hold a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Marine Engineering or a related technical field.
  • Strong curiosity and a genuine interest in understanding how mechanical systems work, fail, and can be improved.
  • Experience in bearing design, calculations, and field performance is an advantage.
  • Strong ability to structure and document technical analyses and findings
  • You possess strong influencing and consulting skills, enabling effective communication with diverse stakeholders.

About the Team

You will join our Bearing Team within the Onshore business unit. The team consists of highly skilled specialists located in Denmark, Germany, Spain, and India. We are responsible for main bearings, blade bearings, and related components across the installed Siemens Gamesa turbine fleet. Your colleagues are passionate about conducting thorough investigations and implementing quality improvements that directly impact our operations and customer satisfaction. Together, you will collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Engineering, Quality, and Service, to drive initiatives that enhance bearing reliability and contribute to the overall success of our projects. Working with us means contributing to long‑term reliability improvements, collaborating across cultures, and playing a vital role in strengthening turbine performance for years to come.

Who is Siemens Gamesa?

Siemens Gamesa is part of Siemens Energy, a global leader in energy technology with a rich legacy of innovation spanning over 150 years. Together, we are committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. As a leading player in the wind industry and manufacturer of wind turbines, we are passionate about driving the energy transition and providing innovative solutions that meet the growing energy demand of the global community. At Siemens Gamesa, we are constantly seeking individuals to join our team and support our focus on energy transformation. Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Gamesa:

Our Commitment to Diversity

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by multiple nationalities. We celebrate character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

Rewards/Benefits

  • Opportunities to work with a global team
  • Medical benefits
  • Remote/Flexible work
  • Paid holidays and parental leave
  • Employer-funded pension
  • Subsidised lunch and more

title: Embedded Software Engineer
description:
At Spectrum Control, most departments operate on a 4-day, 10-hour work schedule in exchange for a 3-day weekend. We offer competitive wages and PTO, plus our benefits begin on day 1 of employment. Come join a workforce where we put you first!

Embedded Software Engineer: The Embedded software engineer designs and implements infrastructure and applications for deploying embedded Linux and supporting software that operate on the most advanced products at Spectrum Control. The Embedded software engineer also develops the functional requirements and testing methodologies to verify system operation.

COMPENSATION RANGE: The expected compensation range for this position is $135,000 - $165,000.00 annually.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

  • Build and deploy the Linux Operating system using the Yocto Build Flow.
  • Maintain software revisions and deployment using tools including GIT and Docker.
  • Develop high-quality embedded application software in C/C++ for ARM-based processors.
  • Develop computer networking software infrastructure.
  • Develop automated test software in C# to control RF test instruments (signal generators, spectrum/network analyzers, power meters) and collect measurement data.
  • Use Artificial Intelligence tools to enhance productivity and problem solve.
  • Derive requirements and verification methods for embedded systems.
  • Produce detailed documentation of system functionality.
  • Provide internal and external customer support as needed.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Education: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or Computer Engineering.
  • Experience Years: 5+ years of embedded software development.
  • Must have expert-level knowledge of the Linux operating system and building embedded Linux systems with Yocto, including custom layers and recipes, BSP integration, kernel configuration, device trees, and U-Boot.
  • Must have strong knowledge of computer networking protocols and tools, and computer architecture.
  • Must have strong C/C++ skills developing embedded software for ARM-based processors, including cross-compilation toolchains, hardware interfaces (SPI, I2C, UART), and debugging with JTAG/GDB.
  • Must have strong scripting skills in Python and Bash for build automation and test tooling.
  • Experience building embedded Linux for Altera or AMD FPGA SoCs preferred.
  • Experience with C#/.NET for test applications preferred.
  • Experience developing instrument control and test automation software using SCPI over VISA (GPIB, LXI/Ethernet, USBTMC) preferred.
  • Knowledge of embedded security practices such as secure boot, encrypted filesystems, and signed software updates preferred.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

  • On-site expectations vary with development phase: during hardware bring-up, integration, and test periods, daily on-site presence at the bench is required; during design and software-focused phases, remote work is supported. Candidates should not expect a fixed weekly hybrid schedule — flexibility follows the needs of the hardware. Travel to our manufacturing facility in Frederick, MD is required at least once per month.
  • This role will be based at one of Spectrum Control's facilities in Marlborough, MA; Philadelphia, PA; Fairview, PA; or Delmar, DE. Candidate should be located within a reasonable commuting distance of one of these locations.

title: LVN, Charge

description:

FHCSD is one of the top 10 largest federally qualified health centers (FQHCs) in the country. We operate more than 90 sites across San Diego County, including 29 primary care clinics, 23 behavioral health facilities, 10 physical rehabilitation clinics, nine dental clinics, five vision clinics, four outpatient substance use treatment programs, three mobile medical units, two mobile counseling centers, two urgent care centers, and a pharmacy.

Our staff provides care to over 227,000 patients each year, of whom 91% are low-income and 29% are uninsured. FHCSD provides care to all. Services include, but are not limited to adult care, chronic disease management, pediatrics, comprehensive women’s care including obstetrics, dental, vision, case management, physical rehabilitation, speech therapy for children, vaccinations, infectious diseases, behavioral health, substance use counseling and a host of specialty services including cardiology, podiatry, endocrinology, dermatology, among others. FHCSD also offers supportive services to those who are unsheltered and in need of intensive case management.

The breadth of our clinic locations, services and programs has grown over the last five decades, making us the largest community clinic provider of health care to the uninsured in the county and one of the top 10 largest community clinic organizations in the nation. We are also the largest health care safety-net provider, largest school-based health care provider and the largest mental health provider in the San Diego region.

Performs a wide variety of patient care activities and accommodative services for assigned clinic patients, as direct by the Clinic Director and/or Nursing Director, in order to facilitate the delivery of prompt, quality care.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively participates in LEAN/HONSHA trainings and serves as a member of the Core Team. Actively participates in other clinical initiatives, such as clinical quality outcomes, to achieve goals and metrics.

  • Builds positive relationships, inspires others to perform at a higher level, prepares career development plans and retains an accountable workforce.

  • Coaches and counsels staff and administers appropriate disciplinary action in a timely manner.

  • Communicates effectively with interdisciplinary care team and support services, including Physicians, PSRs, Medical Assistants, and others. Attends department meetings.

  • Completes all required documentation accurately, in a timely manner, and thoroughly in accordance with department standards; in addition, ensures subordinate staff complete documentation per department standards. Includes documenting patient history.

  • Consistently follows Policies and Procedures to ensure positive patient outcomes.

  • Keeps clinic work-flow moving, focusing on productivity and efficiency, including assigning lunch times and breaks, ensuring exam room is set up, ordering supplies and vaccines to ensure correct supply is on hand, supporting provider productivity, reviewing patient problem list prior to visit with provider, and calling in refills to pharmacy.

  • Keeps site in compliance with TJC, DHS, CHDP, and Medi-Cal Managed Care requirements.

  • Participates in continuous improvement activities and ensures appropriate Lean tools (i.e., 5S, A3) are deployed and results are evaluated and/or measured.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

  • Performs Waive Testing and Phlebotomy if appropriate training has been completed.

  • Provides/ensures staff receive all new hire and annual trainings on time.

Requirements:

  • 3 years of experience in an ambulatory care setting or similar setting preferred.

  • California State Board LVN License required.

  • Current American Heart Association healthcare provider CPR (BLS), or Advanced Cardiac Life Support, Advanced Trauma Life Support, or Advance Resuscitation Training.

  • Graduation from a recognized practical nursing program

  • High School Graduate (or GED equivalent).

  • Traveling between sites and other locations is occasionally required. Must have a valid California driver’s license, an automobile, and proof of minimum levels of car insurance as required under California law, although limits of $100,000 are recommended. An acceptable driving record is also required. California law requires all drivers to obtain a valid California driver’s license within ten days of establishing residency. Reasonable accommodation may be provided on a case-by-case basis. Mileage and other reimbursement governed by policy.

  • Ability to participate collaboratively with multi-disciplinary care team.

  • Ability to work effectively with patients from diverse social, cultural and economic groups.

  • Able to maintain good working relationships with employees, coworkers, and departments.

  • Basic computer literacy ability to comply with department needs and expectations (i.e., electronic medical record documentation, obtaining background information and reports on patients, following up on appts, etc.).

  • Bilingual (Read, Speak & Write) in English/ Spanish preferred.

  • Effective training and coaching skills; ability to drive results and achieve objectives through others.

  • Knowledge of child, adolescent, and adult health care issues.

  • Knowledge of supervisory practices and techniques, including performance management and employee development.

title: Senior Salesforce Reports & Dashboards Developer (with Tableau Reporting)
description:
Senior Salesforce Reports & Dashboards Developer (with Tableau Reporting)1

Key Responsibilities

Business/Functional

  • Partner with business stakeholders (Sales, Service, Marketing, Finance, Operations) to gather reporting requirements and translate KPIs/metrics into report and dashboard specifications.
  • Recommend the right tool and approach for a given need — native Salesforce reports/dashboards vs. Tableau vs. CRM Analytics (Tableau CRM/Einstein Analytics) — based on data volume, audience, refresh needs, and visualization complexity.
  • Define and document data definitions, calculated metrics, and business logic so metrics are consistent and trusted across the organization.
  • Lead requirement walkthroughs and mockup reviews with business users; iterate on wireframes/mockups before build.
  • Provide analytics support during executive/board reporting cycles (QBRs, monthly/quarterly business reviews).
  • Train business users and admins on self-service reporting best practices within Salesforce and Tableau.



Salesforce Reports & Dashboards

  • Design and build custom, complex reports and dashboards in Salesforce: joined reports, matrix/summary reports, cross-filters, bucket fields, custom report types, and dashboard filters/dynamic dashboards.
  • Optimize report and dashboard performance for large data volumes, including use of custom report types, indexed fields, and folder/sharing structures.
  • Configure dashboard subscriptions, scheduled report exports/refreshes, and mobile-friendly dashboard layouts.
  • Manage report/dashboard folder architecture, sharing, and security (role hierarchy, sharing rules) to ensure the right data is visible to the right audience.
  • Build and maintain custom formula fields, roll-up summaries, and (where needed) Apex/Flow-based aggregations to support reporting requirements not achievable natively.
  • Leverage Salesforce reporting APIs (Analytics REST API) for embedding reports/dashboards in external portals or apps where required.



Tableau Reporting

  • Design, build, and maintain Tableau dashboards and visualizations sourced from Salesforce (via Salesforce connector, Tableau Sync/CDC, or ETL) and other enterprise systems (ERP, data warehouse, flat files).
  • Build and optimize Tableau data sources/extracts, including data blending, joins, calculated fields, LODs (Level of Detail expressions), parameters, and table calculations.
  • Design intuitive, performant dashboards following Tableau visualization best practices (appropriate chart types, filters/actions, drill-downs, tooltips, mobile layout).
  • Manage Tableau Server/Cloud publishing, permissions, data source refresh schedules, and workbook version control.
  • Optimize dashboard/query performance (extract vs. live connections, indexing, query optimization) for large datasets.
  • Troubleshoot data discrepancies between Salesforce, Tableau, and other source systems, ensuring a single source of truth for key metrics.



Required Qualifications

  • 5–8 years of overall Salesforce experience, with a strong focus on reporting and analytics (reports, dashboards, custom report types).
  • 3+ years of hands-on Tableau development experience, including Tableau Desktop and Tableau Server/Tableau Cloud (publishing, permissions, scheduling).
  • Deep expertise with Salesforce native reporting tools: joined reports, matrix reports, custom report types, bucket fields, dynamic dashboards, dashboard filters.
  • Solid understanding of the Salesforce data model, object relationships, and security model (roles, profiles, sharing rules) as they relate to reporting visibility.
  • Strong Tableau skills: calculated fields, LOD expressions, parameters, table calculations, data blending/joins, dashboard actions, and performance optimization.
  • Experience connecting Tableau to Salesforce (native connector, Salesforce Sync/CDC, or via a data warehouse/ETL pipeline).
  • Strong SQL skills for data validation, troubleshooting, and building/optimizing underlying data sources.
  • Excellent stakeholder communication skills — able to translate business questions into the right metric, chart, and tool, and to explain data/methodology clearly to non-technical audiences.
  • Experience gathering requirements directly from business stakeholders and iterating on dashboard design based on feedback.



Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with CRM Analytics (Tableau CRM/Einstein Analytics) in addition to native Salesforce reporting.
  • Salesforce certifications: Salesforce Certified Administrator, Salesforce Certified Platform App Builder, or Salesforce Certified Data Cloud/CRM Analytics credentials.
  • Tableau certification (Tableau Desktop Specialist, Certified Data Analyst, or Certified Professional).
  • Experience with ETL/data integration tools (Informatica, MuleSoft, Talend, dbt) and/or a data warehouse (Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery).
  • Familiarity with Python or R for advanced analytics/statistical reporting is a plus.
  • Prior experience in a consulting or shared-services BI/analytics team supporting multiple business units.

title: Solutions Engineer, Channel
description:
Company Background

Censys’ mission is to be the one place to understand everything on the internet. Frustrated by the lack of trustworthy Internet intelligence, we set out to create the industry’s most comprehensive, accurate, and up-to-date map of the Internet. Today, Censys delivers real-time Internet intelligence and actionable threat insights to global governments, over 50% of the Fortune 500, and leading threat intelligence providers worldwide.

Censys is building the most credible, robust map of the Internet through IP scanning, DNS lookups, web crawling, and the ingestion of millions of certificates. Censys was founded by security researchers who are passionate about developing technology that provides anyone the power to fully understand their digital risk and exposure. Individuals and enterprises–and anyone in between–can harness this power to discover new information and insight as the Internet, IoT and Cloud evolve. We are a true security startup with midwestern roots and we believe that a map of the Internet, or a map of your organization’s assets can quickly help guide organizations to the answers they need to protect themselves from vulnerability and risk.

Role Summary

The Channel Solutions Engineer serves as Censys's primary technical resource for channel partners within an assigned region, bridging the gap between complex cybersecurity solutions and partner success. This role combines hands-on pre-sales engineering with strategic partner enablement which includes designing and delivering product demonstrations, designing solution architectures, and creating & leading technical training to help resellers and distributors confidently sell and implement Censys's Internet intelligence platform. Acting as a trusted technical advisor and liaison to internal support teams, the Channel Solutions Engineer drives partner growth by translating technical capabilities into business value, while feeding real-world partner and customer insights back into product strategy.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary technical leader for channel partners within the assigned region
  • Collaborate with focus partners in the territory to develop comprehensive business plans that align to strategic objectives
  • Provide technical pre-sales support to partners, including product presentations, demonstrations and solution architecture design
  • Collaborate with your sales peers to identify opportunities for new partnerships and expand existing ones
  • Plan and drive detailed technical training sessions for partners, ensuring they are proficient in the company’s products, solutions, and integration processes
  • Support channel partners with technical issues during and after product implementation, acting as a liaison between them and the company's technical support teams
  • Applies Business and Technical Acumen to design and deliver customized solutions based on partner and customer needs, ensuring alignment with company standards and best practices
  • Stay updated on product roadmaps, new technologies, and industry trends to better assist partners in growing their business
  • Lead in the development and deployment of channel enablement materials, such as certifications, technical guides, manuals, and webinars
  • Collaborate with the product management and development teams to provide feedback on product improvements based on partner and customer feedback
  • Drives results by maintaining detailed records of partner interactions, sales pipeline, and technical support provided, reporting progress to management regularly
  • Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact
  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in Partner Solution Consulting, pre-sales engineering, or a similar technical role within the technology industry
  • Skilled in at least one of the following Networking, Network Security, Cybersecurity, Private/Public Cloud Security, SOC/Endpoint or SASE
  • Prior experience working with channel is required. Strong understanding of channel sales models and experience working with resellers, distributors, and other channel partners
  • Previous experience selling, implementing, or managing SaaS offerings is strongly preferred
  • Experience in complex sales involving long sales processes with multiple buying centers and multi-product solutions is preferred.
  • Prior experience architecting cybersecurity solutions that solve technical challenges and influence business initiatives is preferred.
  • Experience influencing and gaining buy-in from key stakeholders, either in a customer-facing or internal role
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to present complex technical information to non-technical audiences
  • Hands-on experience with product installations, configurations, and troubleshooting
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a cross-functional team, managing multiple projects in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong problem-solving skills and a proactive attitude towards resolving issues.
  • Willingness to travel within the assigned region to support partners and attend events as necessary
  • Proven track record of influencing key stakeholders and gaining buy-in for technical solutions

For high cost of living areas (San Francisco Bay, New York City, and Seattle), the expected salary range for this position is $220,000 USD - $257,000 USD USD, plus bonus eligibility and equity.

Job level and actual compensation will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process (including skills and prior relevant experience, potential impact, and scope of role), market demands, and specific work location. The listed range is a guideline, and the range for this role may be modified. For roles that are available to be filled remotely, the pay range is localized according to employee work location by a factor of between 83% and 100% of range. Please discuss your specific work location with your recruiter for more information.

Censys offers a competitive benefits package to employees, including equity, health, dental & vision coverage, retirement with company contribution, parental leave, mental health & wellness benefits, flexible PTO, and a professional development stipend. Censys also offers sales incentive pay for most sales roles and an annual bonus plan for eligible non-sales roles. Agency

Texas A&M University

Department

Political Science

Commensurate

College Station, Texas

Staff

Job Description
