title: Project Administrator
description:
About Atkinson

Building our nation's infrastructure since 1926, Atkinson provides innovative design and construction solutions for heavy civil projects. We are committed to safely delivering complex, quality projects while building long-lasting, collaborative relationships with our clients.

The Role

The Project Administrator serves as the support for construction projects and is a primary liaison between operations, corporate finance, and certain external parties. This highly visible and fast-paced position is involved with financial reporting, compliance, and processing responsibilities over projects ranging in size from $20 million to $1 billion in contract value. This position acts as the primary point of contact for communications and responsibilities related to the craft workforce.

Responsibilities

  • Assist with trade/craft payroll processing, collection of timecards and coding. Work with the payroll team on adjustment checks, pay increases, terminations, and per diem packages

  • Process field new hires at the jobsite (dispatching, arranging first day paperwork, drug testing, and safety training)

  • Review certified payroll from subcontractors, manage late certified payroll, and resolve delinquent or missing items directly with Subcontractors

  • Certify and submit Atkinson certified payroll to the owner and DIR

  • Submit and track additional paperwork as required (tax withholdings, fringe benefit statements etc)

  • Process purchase orders and pay project invoices within 30 days of receipt - 3-way match, batching and coding

  • Assist with new vendor setup

  • Assist with monthly pay application (invoice to owner, subcontractor payments, lien waiver collection and tracking).

  • Create, update and maintain various reports and tracking spreadsheets

  • Document control (scanning/uploading documents)

  • Create billing packages with backup for change order work for reimbursement by owner

  • Assist insurance certificate tracking

  • Support general office management and maintain /order office supplies

  • Assist with job site equipment management and inventory control

  • Support relationship management with suppliers, subcontractors, and clients

Qualifications

  • 1-3 Years of administration/accounting experience

  • Demonstrated experience in billing, document control, and purchasing

  • Commitment to maintaining data accuracy and timeliness in processing and delivery

  • Attention to detail

  • Proficient in Microsoft Office, specifically MS Excel and MS Word

  • Experience in Textura, SAP, LCP Tracker or Coupa is preferred but not required

  • Able to work well with others, take direction, and work independently

  • Experience working on large-scale construction projects in a similar role is preferred but not required

  • Strong work ethic and ability to work in a fast-paced team environment

  • Alignment to our Standards of Excellence: self-motivated, results-oriented, adaptable, team player, accountable, ethical, innovative, resilient, builds relationships, builds people/teams and followership, sets direction and executes

The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.

The Physical Side of the Role: Given that a good portion of your day will be spent at a desk, you should be comfortable with prolonged periods of focused work, whether it's collaborating with colleagues, analyzing data, or developing strategies. The role demands effective communication and sharp visual acuity for reviewing complex documents and performing detailed computer work. The ability to lift and move objects up to 10 pounds regularly, and up to 25 pounds on occasion (think a box of files or small office equipment), is also required.

Your Work Environment: Your primary workspace will be in our professional office, which has a typical, quiet-to-moderate noise and light levels. As part of your work, you may also be required to visit active construction sites. These environments are naturally more dynamic and can include exposure to outdoor weather conditions, louder noise, and moving equipment. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Atkinson’s safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations.

Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines. Beyond regular working hours, there will be occasions where business needs require your attention, particularly for time-sensitive matters or emergencies. You are expected to monitor and respond to communications (phone calls, emails, text messages) as required to address these situations effectively. Your ability to manage these expectations and be responsive when critical issues arise is key to your success in this role and our collective success as a team.


A Drug Free Workplace: Clark promotes a drug free workplace. A pre-employment drug “fitness for duty” screening is required, and the company conducts random quarterly drug “fitness for duty” tests.

Atkinson offers a total compensation package that includes base salary, bonus potential, and a comprehensive benefits package including health/dental/vision benefits, paid time off, retirement/401k, and Company Contribution plan. Additional benefits include life insurance, commuter benefit, short & long term disability, fitness reimbursement, FSA, tuition reimbursement, back-up daycare, tutoring & family support benefits, EAP/Work-Life assistance, and a holiday contribution program. For this role the base salary range is $62,400 - 72,800. Compensation may vary outside of this range depending on a number of factors, including a candidate’s education, experience, skills, and geographic location. Base pay is one part of the Total Compensation Package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work.

title: Security Officer - Level I
description:
The primary purpose of the Security Officer is to prevent radiological sabotage and theft of special nuclear material and provide protection of SSES personnel, property and operations against criminal acts.

Primary Responsibilities

  • As a member of the Armed Nuclear Security Force, defend against adversarial actions or threats and prevent radiological sabotage and theft of special nuclear material through the authorized use of deadly or non-deadly force at SSES.
  • Perform access and visitor control, personnel and vehicle searches for contraband and prohibited items, armed security patrols, and escort duties.
  • Control non-licensed and emergency vehicles and conduct visual and electronic surveillance.
  • Respond to alarms and emergency situations, conduct on-scene assessments, and accurately document and report security-related activities.
  • Maintain proficiency with assigned firearms and remain qualified in assigned security duties.
  • Maintain applicable fitness, medical, First Aid, CPR, and other required qualifications throughout employment.

Basic Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Valid Pennsylvania driver’s license. Ability to obtain and maintain REAL ID-compliant identification once required for site access under applicable federal requirements.
  • Valid concealed carry permit, obtained at the employee's expense prior to completion of initial training.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain unescorted access authorization in accordance with applicable NRC and site requirements.
  • Ability to successfully complete and maintain all required security training, firearms qualifications, physical fitness standards, and medical qualifications.
  • Ability to meet applicable Fitness-for-Duty requirements, including required drug and alcohol testing.
  • Ability to effectively communicate verbally and in writing and follow established procedures and instructions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate's degree or higher in Criminal Justice, or prior law enforcement, corrections, security, or military experience.

Additional Information

This position requires working swing shifts, weekends, holidays, overtime, and emergency call-ins as required.

Security Officers must maintain all licenses, permits, certifications, access requirements, and qualifications required for the position throughout employment.

The position requires the ability to perform the physical functions associated with armed security duties, including prolonged standing and walking, responding rapidly to security events, and working in varying indoor and outdoor environmental conditions.

Security Officers must remain alert, exercise sound judgment in high-stress situations, work effectively as part of an armed security team, and respond appropriately to emergency and security-related events.

title: Solution Architect Lead
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Solution Architect Lead based in the United States.

This is a high-impact technical leadership role focused on designing advanced automation and control architectures for mission-critical data center environments.
You’ll serve as a senior technical advisor across customers, consultants, system integrators, OEM partners, sales, product management, and engineering teams.
The role combines deep expertise in PLC-based controls, industrial networking, edge-to-cloud integration, and data center infrastructure.
You’ll shape scalable architectures spanning cooling, electrical systems, energy management, BMS, SCADA, DCIM, and Industrial IoT platforms.
Your work will directly support customers in improving resilience, uptime, operational efficiency, and sustainability.
You’ll also influence product direction, establish technical standards, and help advance emerging capabilities such as AI-driven operations and digital twins.
With up to 30% travel, this position offers the opportunity to work on complex enterprise and hyperscale data center initiatives with significant technical impact.

Accountabilities:

  • Architect and provide application support for advanced PLC-based automation and control solutions supporting data center cooling and other mission-critical applications.
  • Develop scalable control architectures integrating cooling systems, electrical infrastructure, energy monitoring, building management systems, and Industrial IoT platforms.
  • Create reference architectures, solution blueprints, deployment standards, and technical documentation for enterprise-scale implementations.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert on data center infrastructure, including cooling towers, chillers, cooling plants, CRAH/CRAC systems, FDU/CDU equipment, pumping systems, water-side economization, liquid cooling, electrical distribution monitoring, and critical facility alarming.
  • Lead the development and technical review of PLC control strategies using CODESYS and IEC 61131-3 methodologies, including Structured Text, Function Block Diagram, Sequential Function Chart, and Ladder Logic.
  • Support proof-of-concept development, solution validation, demonstrations, field pilots, and deployment activities.
  • Design and validate secure industrial communication architectures using Modbus TCP/IP and RTU, EtherCAT, OPC UA, MQTT, Sparkplug B, Redfish, BACnet/IP, and REST APIs.
  • Ensure interoperability between PLC, SCADA, BMS, DCIM, cloud, and enterprise systems while maintaining appropriate cybersecurity, segmentation, and remote-access practices.
  • Design and support supervisory monitoring and control solutions using Ignition and Ignition Edge, including MQTT and Sparkplug B architectures for enterprise-wide data collection and operational visibility.
  • Act as a trusted technical advisor to customers, consultants, system integrators, and OEM partners through discovery workshops, site assessments, architecture reviews, and solution-envisioning sessions.
  • Support strategic opportunities and complex customer pursuits requiring senior technical expertise and architectural leadership.
  • Partner with Product Management, R&D, Sales Engineering, and Technical Support to influence product strategy, commercialization plans, and technical roadmaps.
  • Gather and communicate Voice of Customer insights to drive product innovation and continuous improvement.
  • Mentor and support technical team members while contributing to best practices, training programs, architecture standards, and technical documentation.
  • Monitor emerging technologies across industrial automation, edge computing, AI-driven operations, digital twins, and data center management to identify opportunities for innovation.

    • Requirements:

    • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Automation Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent industry experience.
    • 10+ years of experience in industrial automation, PLC programming, controls engineering, system integration, solutions architecture, or a related field.
    • Extensive hands-on experience with PLC platforms and industrial control systems.
    • Advanced proficiency with CODESYS development environments and IEC 61131-3 programming methodologies.
    • Demonstrated direct experience with data center infrastructure and mission-critical facility operations, particularly cooling, electrical infrastructure, and facility management systems.
    • Hands-on experience with industrial communication technologies including Modbus TCP/IP and RTU, EtherCAT, MQTT, Sparkplug B, Redfish, OPC UA, and BACnet/IP.
    • Experience designing and deploying Ignition or Ignition Edge solutions.
    • Strong understanding of industrial networking, cybersecurity, network segmentation, and secure remote-access architectures.
    • Experience integrating PLC, SCADA, BMS, DCIM, cloud, and enterprise systems.
    • Excellent communication, presentation, stakeholder management, technical documentation, and customer-facing skills.
    • Ability to translate complex technical requirements into scalable, commercially viable solutions.
    • Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities, with the capacity to work across customers, engineering, product, sales, and partner organizations.
    • Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, Azure, AWS, or edge computing architectures is a plus.
    • Knowledge of machine learning, predictive analytics, digital twins, and operational optimization platforms is advantageous.
    • Experience with large-scale enterprise or hyperscale data center deployments and relevant industry certifications is preferred.
    • Willingness to travel up to 30% for customer engagements, strategic projects, industry events, and demonstrations.

      • Benefits:

      • Competitive salary range of $150,000–$200,000 USD, with placement based on experience and geographic location.
      • Health care coverage.
      • Dental insurance.
      • Vision plans.
      • 401(k) benefits.
      • Commissions and/or incentive compensation, depending on role eligibility.
      • Opportunity to work on complex, mission-critical data center and industrial automation projects.
      • Exposure to emerging technologies including edge computing, AI-driven operations, digital twins, and Industrial IoT.
      • Significant opportunities for technical leadership, customer engagement, innovation, and cross-functional collaboration.

description:

At Wellthy, we dream of a world where everyone has the care infrastructure they need to manage their own health and the health and well-being of their loved ones.

We’re building something new in the care space - reimagining how care is delivered, accessed, and supported by families around the globe. As we grow, we’re seeking collaborative, curious, and purpose-driven teammates to help us expand what’s possible.

We’re building, evolving, and expanding the market category for care, and we’re looking for responsive, collaborative, curious, and purposeful colleagues to join us.

As our People Business Partner, you will you'll be a trusted advisor and coach to managers supporting our hourly, shift-based, in-person workforce — helping them lead well, navigate tough moments with sound judgment, and build a team where people want to stay. You'll bring both strategic thinking and hands-on partnership to the table, balancing employee experience, business needs, and risk as our backup work continues to grow. This is a role for someone who thrives close to the work and wants real ownership over how people are supported.

You will work collaboratively with stakeholders across the business, as well as peers on the broader people team.

Our work is grounded in the expertise of seasoned care professionals who deeply understand families’ real challenges paired with agile, tech-powered solutions that deliver support efficiently and at scale. We embrace a mindset of continuous learning, especially around emerging technologies. Tools like AI and other innovations are accelerators, enabling us to scale our impact, work smarter, and stay at the forefront of care delivery.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role, you’ll need to be open to learning, experimenting, and evolving. Comfort with emerging technology and curiosity around how tools like AI can support your workflow or help families more effectively is a plus.

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience and 4+ years of HR Generalist, People Business Partner, or related experience.
  • Experience supporting an hourly, shift-based, and in-person workforce, with strong understanding of the unique People needs of frontline teams.
  • Experience with employee relations, performance management, benefits, leaves of absence, and other employee lifecycle matters.
  • Strong working knowledge of federal and state employment laws and regulations; experience supporting a multi-state workforce, particularly CA, CO, WA, and/or NY, is a plus.
  • Strong judgment, relationship-building, and communication skills with the ability to navigate complex and sensitive People matters.
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and operate effectively during moments of urgency and change.
  • Curious, resourceful, and solutions-oriented with a willingness to jump in wherever needed and learn new technologies and ways of working.
  • Proven ability to work effectively in a remote Mac environment while supporting distributed and in-person teams.

Total Rewards Package

The starting salary for this position is $90,000-$105,000 annually.

  • Mental health benefits.

Location

title: Rad Tech Supervisor - Stony Point Mammography - Days
description:
The Radiology Technologist Supervisor provides day-to-day supervision for an assigned Radiology area (e.g. Diagnostic, Breast Imaging, Stony Point, CT/MRI, 3D lab) to include STAR Service, legal and regulatory compliance, clinical operations, human resources, safety & quality, customer service, leadership, and fiscal responsibility.

The Radiology Technologist Supervisor ensures that all diagnostic and therapeutic procedures are performed by qualified and competent staff, are of the highest quality achievable and follow the radiation safety principles of ALARA, ACR Guidelines for imaging practices, and ACR Guidelines for MRI Safety, if applicable.Ensure compliance with VCU and VCUHS policies and procedures.

The Radiology Technologist Supervisor works directly with lead technologists and front line staff to solve problems and reduce barriers to success. This job works within the Scope of Practice of his/her specialty. The scope of Practice by specialty is described in the Staff Technologist job description for each specialty. This job also maintains technical competency in all areas of responsibility.

The Radiology Technologist Supervisor implements new initiatives, programs and policies.Work collaboratively with other Radiology Supervisors, Mangers, Faculty and staff to ensure a high level departmental safety, quality, and teamwork.Report to the Modality Manager and is responsible for the clinical functions and processes for assigned Radiology area. Through lead technologists and staff, the Radiology Supervisor is responsible and accountable for the daily clinical operation of the assigned sections by ensuring the highest level of operational excellence while ensuring safety, efficient, high quality and cost effective care. This job supervises, oversees, maintains and improves business functions and processes related to his/her areas of responsibility.Develop staff education and competencies including educational materials, competency forms, etc. This job also provides education to assigned team, students, residents, and other learners.

Licensure, Certification, or Registration Requirements for Hire:
Certification by the American Registry of Radiology Technologist (ARRT) required for Diagnostic Supervisor Plus one of the following specialty registries that is directly related to their department: ARRT in Mammography for Breast Imaging Supervisor, ARRT CT for CT Supervisor, ARRT MRI for MRI Supervisor, ARRT CV or VIR for Interventional Supervisor, ARRT CT or MRI required for 3D lab supervisor, (CI) Cardiac Interventional Radiography, (RCIS) Registered Cardiovascular Invasive Specialist, (RCES) Registered Cardiac Electrophysiology Specialist

Licensure, Certification, or Registration Requirements for continued employment:
Current Certification by the American Registry of Radiology Technologist (ARRT) required for Diagnostic Supervisor
Plus one of the following current specialty registries that is directly related to their department: ARRT in Mammography for Breast Imaging Supervisor, ARRT CT for CT Supervisor, ARRT MRI for MRI Supervisor, ARRT CV or VIR for Interventional Supervisor, ARRT CT or MRI required for 3D lab supervisor, (CI) Cardiac Interventional Radiography, (RCIS) Registered Cardiovascular Invasive Specialist, (RCES) Registered Cardiac Electrophysiology Specialist

Experience REQUIRED:
Minimum of one (1) year of Lead Tech radiologic technology experience.

Minimum of three (3) years of technical experience.

Experience PREFERRED:
Experience performing in a leadership role. Previous work experience in an academic medical center environment.

Education/training REQUIRED:
Graduation from a JRC Accredited Program in Radiologic Technology that is recognized by the ARRT.

Education/training PREFERRED:
Bachelor’s Degree in Clinical Radiation Science, Business, or closely related field from an accredited program is strongly preferred.
Master’s Degree in Health Administration, Business Administration or closely related field from an accredited program is preferred.

Independent action(s) required:
All day to day workflow coordination and team supervision.
Advice and guidance sought from Manager on an as needed situational basis and when there is a major impact on activity of the modality.

Supervisory responsibilities (if applicable):
All team members in assigned modality report to this position; day to day workflow responsibilities may be delegated as appropriate.
Supervisors are expected to cover unplanned absences for staff that may occur on any shift, as needed.

Additional position requirements:
Weekend and other after hours coverage may be required based on workload demand and teaming needs.

title: Project Manager - Consulting
description:
Overview:

  • We are seeking an experienced and results-driven Senior Project Manager with a strong functional and technical foundation in Supply Chain Execution, particularly in Transportation Management Systems (TMS) or Warehouse Management Systems (WMS).

  • Experience leading Blue Yonder (BY) TMS/WMS implementations are highly preferred. The ideal candidate demonstrates a strong sense of urgency, exceptional problem-solving capabilities, and the ability to navigate complex challenges with a "figure-it-out" mindset.

Scope:

  • Building trusted relationships with customers and stakeholders is critical to success in this role. This position is responsible for managing the delivery of large-scale, multi-stream implementation programs for strategic manufacturing clients.

  • The Senior Project Manager will lead geographically distributed teams across multiple workstreams, ensuring successful project execution, governance, customer satisfaction, and business outcomes.

What You'll do:

  • Lead end-to-end delivery of large-scale Supply Chain Execution implementation programs involving TMS or WMS solutions.

  • Manage multiple concurrent workstreams and cross-functional teams across global locations.

  • Establish strong customer relationships and serve as the primary point of contact for project governance, escalations, and delivery oversight.

  • Identify project risks, dependencies, and implementation challenges proactively, and develop mitigation strategies to ensure successful outcomes.

  • Drive adherence to project plans, timelines, budgets, and quality standards while implementing recovery plans when necessary.

  • Leverage functional and technical expertise to guide solution delivery and ensure alignment with customer business objectives.

  • Facilitate collaboration among customer teams, solution architects, technical consultants, integration teams, and executive stakeholders.

  • Manage project financials, including budgeting, forecasting, invoicing, and travel expense management.

  • Monitor project health through governance forums, status reporting, and executive steering committee meetings.

  • Promote a consultative approach to identify opportunities for additional value creation and business growth within existing customer engagements.

  • Mentor and coach project team members, leveraging individual strengths to maximize delivery effectiveness and team performance.

  • Support Agile delivery practices, including sprint planning, backlog prioritization, and iterative project execution.

What we are looking for:

  • 10 to 14 yrs years of experience managing complex Supply Chain Execution projects, specifically Transportation Management Systems (TMS) and Warehouse Management Systems (WMS).

  • Proven track record of delivering large-scale, complex, cloud-based enterprise software implementation projects.

  • Prior experience working as a Functional Consultant, Technical Consultant, Solution Lead, Test Lead or similar role for enterprise supply chain applications.

  • Experience leading enterprise integration projects involving APIs, middleware platforms, integration architecture, and data exchange methodologies.

  • Good understanding of Supply Chain Execution processes, transportation planning, warehouse operations, logistics execution, and order fulfilment

  • Demonstrated expertise in Agile project management methodologies, sprint planning, and hybrid delivery models.

  • Strong stakeholder management, communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills.

  • Proven ability to identify, develop, and optimize team capabilities to ensure successful project delivery.

  • Experience in below tools and technologies preferred

    • Smartsheet

    • Microsoft Project

    • JIRA

    • Salesforce

If you want to know the heart of a company, take a look at their values. Ours unite us. They are what drive our success – and the success of our customers. Does your heart beat like ours? Find out here: Core Values

title: Industritekniker søges – Mazak, CNC og ansvar for produktionen
description:
Som industritekniker bliver du en vigtig del af produktionen, hvor du arbejder med CNC-bearbejdning på både Mazak- og Okuma-centre. Du får ansvar for opsætning, programmering og optimering af produktionen, og du er med til at sikre stabile processer og høj kvalitet.

Arbejdet spænder fra enkeltstyksproduktion til mindre serier, hvor der stilles krav til præcision og forståelse for tolerancer. Du arbejder ud fra tekniske tegninger og foretager løbende justeringer for at sikre optimal drift og effektiv produktion.

Du indgår i et team med høj faglighed, hvor der er fokus på samarbejde og udvikling og hvor din erfaring med forskellige CNC-styringer kommer i spil.

Stillingen er på skiftehold, og det er derfor vigtigt, at du trives med både dag- og aftenarbejde. Man forsøger dog så vidt muligt at placere medarbejdere på daghold, medmindre der er ønske om fast aftenhold


Arbejdsopgaver
  • Programmering og betjening af CNC-maskiner (Mazak og Okuma)
  • Opsætning af værktøj og emner
  • Produktion efter tekniske tegninger
  • Måling og kvalitetskontrol
  • Optimering af processer og køretider
  • Fejlfinding og løbende justering




Faglige Kvalifikationer
  • Uddannet industritekniker eller lignende
  • Erfaring med Mazak, Okuma eller lignende CNC-styringer
  • Erfaring med CNC drej og/eller fræs
  • Kan læse og forstå tekniske tegninger
  • Kendskab til måleværktøj og tolerancer



Personlige kvalifikationer
  • Arbejder struktureret og præcist
  • Kvalitetsbevidst og detaljeorienteret
  • Kan arbejde selvstændigt
  • Mødestabil og ansvarsbevidst
  • Trives med skiftehold



Særlige forhold
  • Arbejdssted: Aalborg-området
  • Arbejdstid: Skiftehold (dag/aften)
  • Opstart: Efter aftale
  • Løn efter kvalifikationer inkl. tillæg
  • Mulighed for fastansættelse

For at komme i betragtning til stillingen sendes CV til aalborg-m@jobteam.dk

Vi afholder løbende samtaler. Men vi venter dog gerne på den rette kandidat.

title: Intern IT - Software Engineer
description:
NiSource Internship Program Introduction

NiSource is currently seeking a Summer IT - Software Engineer Intern. Successful applicants will become integral members of the department while learning within a team environment, completing meaningful tasks and collaborating with team members and leaders on important projects. This position will be a great opportunity for the candidate desiring to launch their career in this field. Successful applicants will build professional relationships with other interns and all levels of NiSource personnel while participating in rewarding professional development exercises and fun, team-building activities. Interns will obtain a broad overview of NiSource's operations and current events in the utilities industry.

This is a 12-week summer internship program starting in May 2027, for students entering their junior or senior year in fall 2027. The role is based in Columbus, OH or Merrillville, IN. Candidates must reside within 50 miles of the reporting location to be eligible.


Essential Functions

  • Enterprise Architecture
    • Enterprise Architecture is responsible for creating the technology strategy and roadmap. This team is responsible for developing standards and guidelines that should be used in planning, designing and implementing Information Technology applications and platforms. This team works collaboratively with other groups to drive the architecture vision for NiSource.
  • IT Services
    • The Services supports the delivery of IT Application and Infrastructure services, including hardware and software asset and configuration management, for all NiSource business units. This role works with the Manager of IT Service Integration, Manager of IT Service Governance and other Technology Tower Leads to ensure that Infrastructure and Application Services are fully integrated and delivered within the scope of Service Provider Contracts as reflected by service levels, statements of work and pertinent schedules/exhibits.
  • Infrastructure
    • Infrastructure, network delivery, primary responsibility is to provide network technical design leadership and to oversee execution of processes associated incident, problem, change, asset, and configuration management within this technology domain. This includes working with enterprise architects, program managers, IT analysts and managed service providers to effectively manage infrastructure operations and support delivery of Infrastructure projects. It also includes development and periodic review of ITIL based processes and practices to ensure highly available operations and compliance with architecture standards and strategies.
  • IT Security
    • The IT Security organization is responsible for the resolution of IT Security incidents; manages preparation & planning for future IT security threats, and follows security trends, threats and vulnerabilities. This role will work on a project to develop and execute a specific cyber incident response scenario exercise and develop a broad-view perspective of the cybersecurity space. Incident response improvement with better Integration of security and IT Operations processes. Work across towers to understand the interrelationships between IT Operations processes, and our company as a whole.
  • IT Applications
  • The IT Applications Developer Job Family encompasses job responsibilities and accountability for various IT applications development, system administration, and support functions necessary to ensure a stable and reliable application environment for NiSource. The application environment encompasses mission critical information systems such as Gas distribution, Hydro and Electrical Grid control systems, Electronic Measurement and other business critical applications. The job also includes the analysis and development of business applications, system interfaces, and other duties related to application system development lifecycle.
  • Business Analytics

• The Business Analytics Intern will leverage their skillset in areas such as data discovery, modeling and visualizing results to identify and discover patterns throughout the business. Through collaboration with business units, this professional will be capable of acquiring, cleansing and structuring data from multiple sources to deliver key analytics based insight to drive business decisions.

  • Acquiring a degree in data science, computer science, computer engineering, statistics, mathematics
  • GPA of 3.0 or higher
  • Have completed at least one year of undergraduate study
  • Experience with cloud, software development, data analytics, automation, or enterprise technologies
  • Keen attention to detail and a quality focused mindset
  • Strong oral and written communication skills
  • Self-discipline for planning and organizing tasks
  • Passionate about data
  • History of being able to learn new technology quickly
  • Solid skills in utilizing computers, operating systems, mobile devices and software (MS Office Suite, MS Project, and other IT applications).
  • Excellent analytical abilities, including process analysis and development, problem-solving and root-cause analysis.
  • Ability to work 40 hours per week

title: Warranty Administrator
description:
Job Summary

The Warranty Administrator is responsible for performing weekly corporate warranty processing and administrative tasks related to fleet equipment. This role follows established policies, procedures, and manufacturer guidelines to
identify, submit, track, and document warranty claims accurately and within required timeframes. The position works closely with corporate support personnel, area fleet support personnel, vendors, and multiple business units to support timely warranty recovery and compliance.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform daily review of maintenance records, work orders, and repair activity to identify potential warranty claims.

  • Prepare, submit, and track warranty claims in accordance with GFL policies and manufacturer requirements.

  • Maintain accurate and complete warranty documentation, including claim details, supporting materials, and correspondence.

  • Enter and update warranty information in the Company’s maintenance system (M5) and other required tracking tools.

  • Use multiple OEM and manufacturer warranty systems to process and monitor claim status.

  • Update and maintain tracking logs using Google Sheets to monitor deadlines, approvals, and resolutions.

  • Follow up with vendors, manufacturers, and internal teams to obtain required information and ensure timely claim completion.

  • Communicate claim status updates to appropriate stakeholders as needed.

  • Perform work in a fast-paced environment while meeting strict submission and follow-up deadlines.

  • Adhere to established processes, workflows, and standard operating procedures related to warranty administration.

  • Perform other related administrative duties as assigned within the scope of warranty.

Knowledge, Skills & Competencies

Technical Skills:

  • Proficiency in Google Workspace tools (Sheets, Docs, Etc)

  • Understanding of AI tools integration, uses, and limitations (Google Gemini)

Behavioral Competencies

  • Collaboration, problem-solving, communication.

  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

  • Ability to work effectively with multiple business units.

Requirements

  • Prefer a minimum of one (1) year of experience working with fleet parts, heavy-duty equipment, and/or diesel or CNG trucks.

  • Basic working knowledge of truck and body systems, including: Engine, aftertreatment, braking, suspension, cooling systems, electrical, diesel and CNG fuel systems, hydraulic, pneumatic, and related components.

  • Basic working knowledge of refuse body types and operational basics.


Interfaces & Stakeholders

  • Collaborates with vendors, manufacturers on proper processing procedures, adheres to guidelines set by warranty agreements and communicates those to the field.

  • The internal team communicates with multiple levels of business and is responsible for processing warranty between the maintenance level and OEM partners in a timely manner.

  • Provide data and guidance to corporate directors as requested in a clear and concise manner that would be visible by upper management and shareholders.

Physical Demands

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position for 75% of the workday.

  • Occasional walking, standing, and ability to move around the office.

  • Use of hands for typing, data entry, grasping, pinching, and operating standard office equipment


Working Conditions & Travel

  • Office work environment

  • In-Office Preferred, work from home on as needed basis.

  • Limited travel may be required for training or presentations.

title: Commercial Underwriting Specialist, Construction
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Commercial Underwriting Specialist, Construction based in Canada.

As a Commercial Underwriting Specialist, you will manage and service increasingly complex construction risks while balancing sound underwriting judgment with strong client relationships.
You’ll evaluate and negotiate renewal rates, assess risk exposures, and develop tailored insurance solutions within established guidelines.
The role offers direct exposure to a broad broker network and requires proactive communication across email, phone, and in-person meetings.
You’ll contribute to business objectives while maintaining high standards for data quality and service levels.
As a senior member of the team, you’ll also coach and mentor junior underwriters and share your expertise.
You’ll work in a collaborative environment with opportunities to expand your knowledge and appetite for complex commercial risks.
This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact supporting Canadian businesses through thoughtful, relationship-driven underwriting.

Accountabilities:

  • Underwrite and service increasingly complex commercial construction accounts in line with established underwriting guidelines and business objectives.
  • Execute renewal rates, evaluate risk, and negotiate appropriate pricing based on account characteristics and market conditions.
  • Develop practical, solutions-oriented approaches to complex underwriting needs while maintaining appropriate risk discipline.
  • Build and maintain strong, professional relationships with brokers and customers through responsive and proactive communication.
  • Work closely with the broker network to understand client needs and develop customized insurance solutions.
  • Maintain national standards for data quality and service level agreements across assigned accounts.
  • Participate in broker meetings, including regular in-person interactions, to strengthen relationships and support business development.
  • Coach and mentor junior underwriters, sharing technical knowledge and helping strengthen the team's underwriting capabilities.
  • Collaborate with experienced underwriters and colleagues to continuously develop expertise in complex commercial risks.

    • Requirements

    • 5+ years of commercial underwriting experience, with specific experience in construction risks.
    • Completed or actively pursuing a CIP or FCIP designation; additional insurance qualifications are an asset.
    • Strong knowledge of commercial underwriting principles, including renewal pricing, risk evaluation, negotiation, and account servicing.
    • Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain effective professional relationships with brokers and/or customers.
    • Strong sales, negotiation, communication, and customer service capabilities.
    • Solutions-oriented mindset with sound judgment and the ability to work effectively with increasingly complex accounts.
    • Strong interpersonal skills and confidence communicating through email, phone, and in-person meetings.
    • Experience coaching or mentoring junior colleagues is highly valued.
    • Team-first mentality with the ability to collaborate effectively in a professional, fast-paced environment.

title: Research Scientist Intern
description:
Pluralis Research works on Protocol Learning: training and serving large models in a fully decentralized way on small consumer-grade devices connected via the internet. Despite being dismissed as infeasible, we have made significant advances on this problem, most recently Agora, a permissionless run that pretrained an 8B model from scratch on consumer GPUs spread over the internet, with no single participant ever holding the full weights (tech report). While many of the core research problems have been solved, Protocol Learning unlocks a series of new challenges. For the mission in full, read A Third Path: Protocol Learning.

This setting breaks nearly every assumption of datacenter training and inference: communication-efficient training across different parallelism axes, fault tolerance as nodes join and drop mid-run, heterogeneous compute and networks, and robustness to malicious participants. Our published methods include Subspace Networks, Factored Gossip DiLoCo, AsyncMesh, and Sentinel.

As a Research Scientist Intern you join us for a 6-month, fixed-term research internship during your PhD, focused on publishing. You work on the problems that stay open as we push from the 8B run toward frontier scale, with access to significant compute and focused mentorship from senior scientists. These are foundational papers up for grabs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Publish in Tier-1 venues: Conduct novel research in Protocol Learning with the explicit goal of publishing in tier-1 ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR).

  • Own a real problem: Pick a question that blocks Protocol Learning at scale and answer it — the internship is scoped so a foundational paper is a realistic outcome, not a stretch goal.

What We're Looking For

  • Publication track record (required): Current PhD candidate with at least one publication in top-tier ML venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR).

  • Research focus: You work in a core technical area relevant to frontier models.

  • Technical depth: Strong theoretical understanding of deep learning and distributed systems principles.

  • Implementation skills: Proficiency in PyTorch and experience with large-scale training infrastructure.

  • Mission alignment: You believe Protocol Learning is the viable third path for collective, trustless, and sovereign AI.

FYI's

  • This is a 6-month, fixed-term research internship. We only hire in Australia and the US, and visa sponsorship is limited to these countries.

  • We work remotely across the world, with the main teams in Australia and North America. You'll need to be comfortable working across timezones.

  • Applicants must have professional-level English proficiency (written and spoken).

title: Product Owner (Mechanical)
description:
Do you want to join one of the world’s leading process technology companies in a role where you take ownership of a product from design to the finished manufactured component? At GEA, your decisions will shape both core products as well as project outcomes – all while working with cutting-edge technologies and a skilled engineering team that values communication, collaboration and technical excellence.

Responsibilities / Tasks

In this central role, you will act as the one point of contact for your components and ensure that the components meet all requirements throughout their lifecycles - from design, compliance and documentation to purchasing, workshop follow-up, and ensuring quality of manufacturing of the final component. You will be involved and hands-on with projects, from sale tenders to final product implementation.

You will collaborate with project managers and Sales to find the best solution, whereafter you will be responsible for developing design and drawings in collaboration with our engineering teams here in Søborg and in India.

You will then initiate the procurement in coordination with our purchasing department and subsequently interact with workshops. Together with the QC department, you will ensure the quality of the final product, both locally and globally, as well as support our commissioning teams around the world. Your primary tasks will include:

  • Project-specific design customization and check of nozzle system for spray drying equipment, for dairy, food and chemical
  • Develop designs of 3D models and manufacturing drawings using Inventor and Vault, in collaboration with our design teams in Denmark and India
  • Standardization, optimization, and further development of products
  • Preparation of documentation such as technical manuals, risk assessments, and ensure compliance, etc.
  • Component inspections at workshops
  • Close collaboration and communication with sales, project management, product management, procurement, QC, as well as workshops to follow up on projects

The work primarily takes place at the office in Søborg, with assistance in project execution and workshops. Travel to sites and workshops is expected to be around 5-20 days per year.

Your Profile / Qualifications

In this role high independence, proactivity and initiative is expected, which also means you will have a strong influence on your daily work and tasks.

We expect that you are ready to take ownership and coordinate across multiple stakeholders. You are structured, self-driven and thrive in taking responsibility throughout a project. At the same time, you are great at communication and collaboration both within your team and across departments and functions.

Furthermore, we imagine that you:

  • Are a trained mechanical engineer or similar with strong background within manufacturing processes and stainless-steel sheet metal material knowledge
  • Are experienced with CAD, preferably Autodesk Inventor and Vault
  • Have experience with High Pressure equipment, with knowledge about PED
  • Have experience with equipment design standards and hygienic design
  • Preferably have experience with large processing equipment.
  • Are fluent in Danish and English, spoken as well as written.

GEA Group – Engineering for a better world
At GEA, we provide cutting-edge equipment and project solutions to the chemical, pharmaceutical, food, and dairy industries. With 18,000+ employees across 62 countries, we specialize in sustainable, efficient solutions that optimize production and reduce environmental impact.

At our site in Søborg, you will join our Centre of Competence Engineering department where 50 dedicated and highly skilled engineers and technicians, work on both standard and customer-specific process equipment. In this department, you will be part of a team with 8 other engineers that have ownership and are responsible for technology such as Fluid bed drying and Spray drying, used for drying pharma and chemical products.

Would you like to know more?

If you would like to find out more about this position before submitting your application, please do not hesitate to contact:

  • Senior Manager Spray Drying & Atomization Technologies, Asger Hansen, asger.hansen@gea.com
  • Senior Director Centre of Competence Drying Technology, Sten Krog Duerlund, sten.duerlund@gea.com

title: Service Agreements Controller
description:
Company :

Truck Stops (NZ) Ltd

Join our team and play a key role in delivering service agreements that keep our customers’ commercial vehicles on the road.

We’re looking for a Service Agreements Controller to support the management of our Service Agreement programme. This is a varied role combining customer service, contract administration, financial analysis and coordination across our branches, dealers and sales teams.

What you’ll be doing

  • Manage Service Agreement quotes, pricing, approvals and contracts.
  • Monitor vehicle servicing, repairs and maintenance against contract requirements.
  • Review invoices, costs and contract performance to ensure agreements remain commercially viable.
  • Monitor vehicle kilometres and manage adjustments, including excess kilometre invoicing.
  • Prepare customer proposals, tenders and monthly reports.
  • Work closely with branches, dealers, sales teams and customers to resolve issues and keep agreements running smoothly.
  • Support continuous improvement, training and initiatives that improve customer service and vehicle uptime.

What we’re looking for
You’ll be organised, commercially minded and detail-focused, with strong communication skills and the ability to build effective relationships across the business.

Ideally, you’ll bring:

  • Experience in contract administration, service administration, fleet, automotive or a similar environment.
  • Strong numerical and analytical skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills.
  • Confidence working with data, systems and reporting.
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills.
  • A proactive approach and willingness to identify ways to improve processes.
  • The ability to work independently while being a great team player.

Automotive or commercial vehicle industry experience is an advantage, but we’re also interested in people with strong transferable skills and the right attitude.

Why join us?

This is a great opportunity to join a team where you’ll have a direct impact on customer experience, vehicle uptime and the success of our Service Agreement programme.

Above all you’ll be a team player who understands embraces our company values – Act with Integrity, Care for All, Win Together.

We offer you

  • A comprehensive privileges programme that includes discount purchasing across 100+ retailers & companywide discounts
  • Ongoing training and development opportunities, including paid study leave
  • Regular team events and a great workplace culture

About Us

Truckstops is a wholly owned subsidiary of Sime Motors. Established in 1984, Truckstops has provided unparalleled after-sales parts and service support to the road transport industry for over 30 years.

With 19 nationwide branches supporting Hino, Mack, UD Trucks and Volvo Truck & Bus, we have grown to become the largest supplier of truck & bus parts and workshop services in New Zealand.

title: Mammography Tech - Adult Outpatient - Days
description:
**$20,000 Sign On Bonus for offers accepted by September 31 2026. Terms and Conditions apply**

The practice of mammography is performed by radiologic technologists who have initially met the qualifications to administer ionizing radiation. The technologist must subsequently have met the federal mammography training requirements as specified in the Mammography Quality Standards Act of 1992 (MQSA). A mammography technologist performs radiographic procedures and related techniques, producing images at the request of and for interpretation by a licensed independent practitioner. Mammography integrates scientific knowledge, technical skills, patient interaction and compassionate care to obtain viable diagnostic information. A mammography technologist recognizes patient conditions essential for successful completion of a procedure.

Radiographers must demonstrate an understanding of breast anatomy, physiology, pathology, and medical terminology. Mammography technologists must comprehend the complexities of the federal regulations in or der to meet the minimum standards for the performance of mammography. He or she must have knowledge of quality assurance policies and quality control testing for digital mammography. Mammography technologists must maintain a high degree of accuracy in breast positioning, exposure techniques, and subsequent evaluation of imaging parameters to optimize patient imaging and care while adhering to radiation protection and safety standards.

Mammography technologists are the primary liaison between patients, licensed independent practitioners, and other members of the support team. Mammography must remain sensitive to the physical and emotional needs of the patient through good communication, assessment, monitoring, and care skills. Participation in quality improvement processes and continuous assessment of performance is expected.

The scope of practice for the Mammography Technologist includes:
Performing breast imaging procedures.
Determining radiographic technique exposure factors.
Performing radiography of pathologic breast specimens.
Providing or assisting with physical breast inspection or palpation.
Assisting LIP breast interventional radiographic procedures.
Applying the principles of patient safety during all aspects of radiographic procedures, including assisting and transporting patients.
Receiving, relaying, and documenting verbal, written, and electronic imaging orders in the patient’s medical record.
Corroborating patient’s clinical history with the ordered procedure while ensuring information is documented and available for use by a licensed independent practitioner (LIP).
Verifying informed consent.
Assuming responsibility for patient needs before, during, and after procedures.
Preparing patients for procedures.
Applying principles of ALARA to minimize exposure to patient, self, and others.
Performing venipuncture per procedural protocol based on imaging order from a licensed independent practitioner.
Starting and maintaining intravenous access per procedural protocol based on an imaging order for a LIP.
Identifying, preparing, and /or administering medications generally associated with diagnostic imaging procedures as prescribed by a LIP.
Evaluating images for technical quality, ensuring proper identification is recorded.
Identifying and escalating emergency situations and managing until appropriate LIP, EMS, MERT, RRT, or Code Team arrives to assume control.
Providing patient education related to imaging procedure.
Educating, mentoring, and general oversight of students and other learners in the Radiology environment.
Performing ongoing quality assurance activities.

Licensure, Certification, or Registration Requirements for Hire: Registry by the American Registry of Radiology Technologist (ARRT-R) ARRT-M Licensure, Certification, or Registration Requirements for continued employment: Current Certification by ARRT in Radiography Current Certification by ARRT in Mammography (ARRT-M) Basic Life Support (BLS for Healthcare Providers) Experience REQUIRED: One (1) year of previous work experience as Breast Imaging Technologist Experience PREFERRED: One to three (1-3) year of previous work experience as Breast Imaging Technologist Previous work experience in an academic medical center environment Education/training REQUIRED: Graduation from a JRC Accredited Program in Radiologic Technology that is recognized by the ARRT Education/training PREFERRED: Bachelors Degree in Radiologic Technology or closely related field from an accredited program Independent action(s) required: The mammography technologist utilizes independent professional judgment to obtain the resultant diagnostic information when possible and seeks directive from a qualified interpreting physician or lawful institutional policies (or standards of care) to continue to discontinue the exam otherwise. Mammography Technologists independently performs screening and diagnostic mammography exams based on lawful institutional policies and/or practice standards and/or follows the directive of the interpreting physician to assist in the completion of the exam. Mammography Technologists represent the goals, values, and vision of VCU Health System. Ensures adherence to regulatory standards, health system and department policies, procedures, processes, and guidelines applicable to role. Resolves basic service delivery issues. Lead technologists may perform “lead technologist” functions such as coordinating work assignments, workflow, and staffing for an assigned shift/area; serve as clinical or technical resource; provide training. Supervisory responsibilities (if applicable): N/A Additional position requirements: Individual shift rotation and schedules will be established with your specific manager or supervisor. Schedules, including requirements of shift rotations and hours of work may be adjusted as necessary to meet staffing needs of the health system. Weekend and other after hours coverage may be required based on workload demand and staffing needs of the health system. Mammography Technologists are considered “Essential Employees” who may be required to report to work in accordance with the VCUHS Policy. Age Specific groups served: All Physical Requirements (includes use of assistance devices as appropriate): Physical: Lifting 20-50 lbs. Other: describe - Activities: Prolonged standing, Prolonged sitting, Walking (distance), Repetitive motion, Other: Prolonged computer interaction Mental/Sensory: Strong recall, Reasoning, Problem solving, Hearing, Speak clearly, Write legibly, Reading, Logical thinking, Other: Vision Emotional:Fast pace environment, Able to handle multiple priorities, Frequent and intense customer interactions, Noisy environment, Able to adapt to frequent change

Compensation Ranges:

Mammography Technologist I: $33.00 - $48.70
Mammography Technologist II: $33.00 - $48.70
Mammography Technologist III: $35.19 - $54.55

Actual Salary offers will be based on several key factors to include relevant work experience, credentials, and qualifications.
